title: Street Sports Basketball
build: XPB disk, Scratch of Triangle directory

records.c: Direction register of the processor port. The match initialization at $0EC6 writes $2F before changing the banking state in $01.
CPU port data register. The overlay selects KERNAL and I/O with $37 around disk loads. The page exchange uses $24 to reach RAM under I/O.
Highest active slot. Setup writes six for the players and the update loop decrements from this value through the ball at zero.
Sign-clear side's computer decision counter. Each side increments its own entry at $4CC9. The checks test low bits to spread decisions across updates.
Second computer decision count, indexed with one at the base address $03 when the actor's side sign is set.
Current possessor slot. The controlled-actor fire handler at $2237 skips the player switch and clears its hold count if the active slot matches this byte.
Side flags of the selected actor. The nearest uncontrolled opponent scan compares candidate flags with this byte and replaces it with the chosen slot's flags.
Target slot saved by the ball-velocity entry at $5096. The velocity solver reads it again at $535B.
Controlled slot on the sign-clear side. The actor control dispatcher compares the active slot against it before choosing a control path.
Controlled slot on the sign-set side. The paired update at $2152 installs a selected teammate for this side.
Scratch low byte of the scaled movement component in the direction multiply at $2098. The restart handler also uses it for the first height threshold.
Paired high movement component from the direction multiply. During the restart height check it instead contains the second threshold.
Working low horizontal difference in the actor distance routine. If the difference is negative with high byte $FF, the routine complements this byte before halving it.
Active actor slot during the roster update. The input dispatcher, fire counter and several action handlers reload it after using Y for table indexing.
Low byte of the committed court camera origin. Draw code uses this coordinate after the new scroll position is published.
High byte of the committed camera origin. The object projection subtracts it with borrow from the low-byte subtraction.
Proposed low byte of the camera origin. The two directional paths update it by the step in $15, then clamp and publish it.
Proposed high byte of the camera origin. It receives carry or borrow from the camera low-byte update.
Committed low three bits of the horizontal camera position. The update stores the candidate phase from $14 here after it prepares the scroll state.
Candidate fine-scroll phase, from masking the proposed camera position with seven at $34C0.
Camera step size. Starts at two and is replaced by one near an edge of the ball-follow window.
Minimum distance for the sign-clear side in the two-side scan. The uncontrolled-opponent scan also uses it as its running best distance.
Minimum distance for the sign-set side in the two-side scan. It starts at $FF before comparing the actors on that side.
Actor index paired with the sign-clear distance at $16. It changes when the scan accepts a closer actor or a tie.
Actor index paired with the sign-set distance at $17. The selected actor is written at $3B3E.
Ball X in eight-pixel steps. $2587 shifts the two-byte X coordinate three times into this byte.
Ball depth in four-pixel steps. The cache at $259D saves it for computing restart placements.
Oscillator byte sampled at $1EBF for the computer direction path. The later branch reads this saved sample.
Restart side sign. The placement paths compare it with an actor's flag sign to choose the direct or mirrored column calculation.
Ball action phase. $1923 advances the state and the collision handler can write the score-detection phase $50 here.
Ball contact and restart selector. The basket award treats its sign as a side flag and the ball reset handler also uses it as a placement index.
Selected restart slot. The restart driver uses it to initialise or steer the actor, and later decrements it while the roster settles.
Ball action delay used by the restart and scoring phases. The current phase can initialise the count, decrement it or test for zero.
Workspace used as the low portion of the motion projection at $22DF. Direction scaling and target selection also reuse the byte.
Fractional result byte of the first projected coordinate, accumulated by $22EA–$22EE.
Next byte of the accumulated first projected coordinate. The carry from $22EA enters the addition at $22F0.
Low multiplier word byte during directional movement. The heading-reference routine also saves the reference slot or its X fraction here.
High multiplier word byte during directional movement. In the coordinate comparison routine it instead holds the reference X low integer byte.
High integer byte of the reference actor's X position at $5B30. The target projection also uses this byte for its accumulator.
Scratch X velocity fraction in the target projection. The heading calculation uses it for the reference depth fraction.
Scratch integer X velocity in the projection. At $5B3A the coordinate comparison also reuses it for reference depth.
Sign extension of the projected X velocity word, set to zero or $FF before the multiply.
Fractional depth velocity used in the projection. The reference-coordinate path reuses it for the horizontal velocity's extension byte.
Integer depth velocity in the projection, saved before multiplying projected displacement.
Sign extension of the projected depth velocity. $22A1 initializes it to zero and $22C1 handles the negative case.
Source pointer low byte for the initial screen copy. The setup steps it by forty after each row.
Source pointer high byte for the initial screen copy. The right-half pass starts this pair in page $E4.
Destination pointer low byte for the initial court screen and colour writes. It is advanced by one 40-cell row at a time.
Destination pointer high byte for setup. The colour copy temporarily substitutes the matching page in the colour RAM window.
Initial court colour-source pointer low byte. The left-half setup advances this pair by eighty for each source row.
Initial court colour-source pointer high byte. Setup uses page $E8 at the start of the colour copy.
Slot saved by the controlled-actor refresh at $2155. The candidate scan reloads it before comparing the next actor.
Green score's low two packed decimal digits. The award path increments them by two and propagates decimal carry.
Green score's hundreds digit. The printer at $1517 reads it separately from the packed low digits.
Blue score's low two packed decimal digits. The store at $55B0 puts the incremented result here.
Blue score's hundreds digit. It receives carry from the decimal addition to $39.
Screen column where the green numeric score starts. The panel setup saves it after printing the team's name.
Screen column where the blue numeric score starts. The refresh routine loads it at $1526.
Computer controller enable for the sign-clear side. The fire test uses the synthetic count at $3F when this byte is nonzero.
Computer controller enable for the sign-set side. The fire test uses $40 for this side when enabled.
Synthetic fire count for the sign-clear side. $68D5 increments it, and the controller path tests it for nonzero at $690D.
Synthetic fire count for the sign-set side, tested at $692E. It can also increment when the other side's count wraps.
Fire override for the sign-clear side. A negative value forces clear carry and a positive value forces set carry.
Fire override for the sign-set side. Zero lets the normal computer or hardware fire check run.
Candidate comparison workspace. During the projection pass $4EA5 saves the fine distance here before selecting an alternate candidate.
Direction workspace for the computer target scan. $4EAB stores the eight-way code made from its 24-way bearing.
Fine direction workspace. The target scan saves the initial heading at $4D26 and changes it while testing neighboring bearings.
Coarse distance recorded by the computer pass selector from the result in $9D.
Fine bearing saved by the pass selector. It is used when comparing candidates and mapped to a joystick direction after acceptance.
Pass selection state. It starts at one and is adjusted by the two entry paths at $675B and $6765 before choosing an option.
Sign-clear side's computer action latch. The pass selector writes two here and other actions can set different countdown values.
Sign-set side's companion computer action latch, indexed from the base at $49.
First side's candidate countdown. The fallback starts it at six and the search decrements the side's indexed entry.
Second side's companion candidate countdown, initialized alongside the first at $128B.
First side's projection-result balance. The scan starts it at zero and increments or decrements it when testing alternate paths.
Second side's projection-result balance. The pass selector reads it as $4D,X with X equal to one.
First side's first comparison flag. It can be reset to zero or marked with $80 by the projection branch.
Second side's first comparison flag, indexed with one from the base at $4F.
First side's second comparison flag. $4ECC stores the result paired with the flag in $4F.
Sign-set side's companion second comparison flag, indexed from the base at $51.
Projected target-distance score from the table at $4F4A. The fallback uses six when the preferred lookup is unavailable.
Primary input setting byte for the sign-clear side. Match setup writes it using the table at $0F07 for that side's choice.
Primary input setting byte for the sign-set side. $1263 reads its value from $0F07 before writing it here.
Secondary input setting for the sign-clear side, selected by the same controller index from $0F0D.
Secondary input setting for the sign-set side, written by the setup path after $1268.
Winning side sign used during the match-end presentation. The target comparisons choose zero for the first score and $80 for the second.
Distance score for the target selected by the rank scan. The result is written at $33EF and follow-through branches compare it with their range thresholds.
Low byte of the current source row pointer for horizontally shifting the screen window.
High byte of the current source row pointer, including borrow in the left-shift path.
Low byte of the destination row pointer, one cell left or right of the source.
High byte of the destination row pointer. The right shift includes any carry from adding one to the low byte.
Low byte of the nonzero estimate for the horizontal vector. The scaler repeatedly shifts it with its high byte at $5F.
High byte of the horizontal distance estimate. $532B saves it from the sum of the two adjusted component magnitudes.
Working low byte of the distance estimate during the five smaller increments in the component scaling loop.
Working high byte of the distance estimate. The refinement loop adds or subtracts the step from $5E/$5F along with any carry or borrow from $60.
Selected target index from the scan at $33ED. The ball velocity path distinguishes a negative result from a slot or other nonnegative target.
Eight-way heading of the selected target. $33E8 saves the returned direction code when the scan accepts a new best candidate.
Low byte of the selected 17-cell court column address. The ball and actor contact lookups read through this pair.
High byte of the court column pointer, loaded from the high-byte view of the table at $468E.
Column within the current contact tile, masked to an eight-pixel range. Shape handlers compare it with local depth.
Row within the current contact tile. The handler at $3F40 uses row minus four to select the upper-half lookup.
Scratch contact offset used while forming the shape-table index. The contact handler also saves its signed response here.
Fractional scratch result in the mixed-axis rebound. The handler at $42ED begins by shifting one horizontal word into this low byte.
Fractional scratch result for the second rebound component at $4307.
Integer scratch result paired with $6A in the rebound calculation.
Current voice 1 effect phase. The dispatcher at $270E uses it to select the next effect action.
Current voice 2 effect phase, read by the dispatcher at $288B.
Low byte of the voice 1 frequency change word. The phase setup at $2748 seeds this field.
High byte of the voice 1 frequency change word. Some phase entries use $FF for a downward change.
Base frequency low byte for the second SID voice's sweep helper.
Base frequency high byte for the voice 2 sweep. $2B6F adds the offset's high part and the low-byte carry.
Low byte of the second SID voice's per-tick frequency sweep step.
High byte of the voice 2 sweep step. The accumulated offset gets it with carry from the low-byte addition.
Accumulated voice 2 sweep offset low byte.
Accumulated voice 2 sweep offset high byte. The start handlers clear or seed it with the low byte.
Delay for stepping the voice 1 effect phase. The phase launcher sets it before activating the next stage.
Countdown for the second voice effect. Several handlers use it to decide when to advance or silence the voice.
Outer timer of the alternating second-voice pulse sweep. The start sets it to $3C and the down phase decrements it.
Scratch copy of the current slot's fractional X byte, loaded at $1401.
Temporary low integer X for the current slot, paired with $7B and read as a target coordinate by distance routines.
Temporary high integer X. The actor update puts the active slot's high byte here at $140E.
Scratch copy of the current slot's fractional depth byte, loaded before the integer depth.
Temporary integer depth. $1418 puts the active slot's depth here, and target selection can replace it for the distance scan.
Scratch copy of the active slot's fractional height from $0234,Y.
Scratch copy of the active slot's integer height from $023D,Y.
Scratch copy of the active slot's fractional X velocity.
Scratch copy of the active slot's integer X velocity.
Scratch copy of the active slot's fractional depth velocity.
Scratch copy of the active slot's integer depth velocity.
Scratch copy of the active slot's fractional vertical velocity.
Scratch copy of the active slot's integer vertical velocity.
Temporary heading for the active slot. The update loop loads $027E,Y here and writes the value back after the control calls.
Temporary copy of the active slot's $028C byte. The routine sends it back at $1474.
Current placement or pose selector. The placement dispatcher doubles it for its jump table and the pose lookup uses it as its within-row offset.
Selected direction and control byte for the active slot. The actor dispatch stores it from one of the inputs and the update writes it back to $029A,Y.
Active actor's side and action flags copied from $02A1,Y. Its sign selects the side's counters and overrides.
Active actor pose-state scratch. The main update loads the pose state at $0200,Y into this byte.
Coarse reference X in heading calculations. It can be built from the active actor's X divided by eight or shifted by the scripted steering bias.
Companion coarse reference depth. The scripted movement path scales the integer depth by four before saving it here.
Coarse target column supplied to the heading quantizer. The scripted actor movement loads it from $02CD,Y.
Coarse target row supplied to the heading quantizer. Scripted movement takes it from $02D4,Y.
Magnitude of the coarse horizontal coordinate difference. The quantizer compares it with the magnitude at $93.
Magnitude of the coarse depth difference, written at $92,X with X equal to one.
Sign marker for the horizontal difference. The coarse bearing routine uses it when choosing the first or second pair of sectors.
Sign marker for the depth difference, read by the sector branches at $2603 and $261B.
Axis order flag. Zero records that X was smaller, while one says that X was at least as large.
Smaller of the two coarse coordinate magnitudes. It limits the trial additions in the ratio loop.
Larger coarse magnitude. The distance routine uses it first, then the bearing ratio loop shifts this byte right.
Accepted trial magnitude so far in the coarse ratio approximation. A trial that reaches the smaller component is skipped.
Accepted trial weight in the coarse ratio approximation, later reduced to a direction step from zero to three.
Current trial weight in the coarse ratio loop, starting at eight and halving after each comparison.
Fine bearing returned by $25B4. Its range of 24 directions is mapped to an eight-way input direction by callers.
Distance estimate calculated with the fine bearing. $25B4 also returns the estimate in X.
Sum of the two coarse magnitudes when it fits in a byte. The distance estimate uses it in the three-quarter calculation.
Rounded coarse X for the actor indexed by Y in the heading comparison. The helper divides the rounded position by eight and adds $20.
Rounded coarse depth for the actor indexed by Y. The conversion divides by four and adds $40.
Rounded coarse X for the actor indexed by X, used as the second coordinate in the heading comparison.
Rounded coarse depth of the actor indexed by X. The axis-difference helper compares it with $A0 on the second call.
Absolute horizontal difference between the actor coordinates. The quantizer loads it into X before ordering the two magnitudes.
Absolute depth difference, stored at $A3 plus one by the second axis call.
Marker $80 for a negative horizontal difference or zero otherwise.
Marker for a negative depth difference. The bearing calculation reads it for the sector within the horizontal sign pair.
Comparison flag for axis order in the actor heading search. The branch sets it to one when X is at least as large.
Smaller actor coordinate magnitude, used as the upper limit for ratio trial additions.
Larger actor coordinate magnitude. The approximate distance reads it before the ratio calculation shifts it.
Trial magnitude accumulator for the actor ratio loop. It keeps only additions below the smaller magnitude.
Trial weight total for the actor ratio. The reduction routine replaces it with the final step.
Current actor ratio trial weight, starting at eight and shifting once per cycle.
Starting sector and then final 24-way bearing for the actor heading calculation.
Distance estimate returned in X by the actor heading quantizer.
Sum of the two actor coordinate magnitudes when addition does not overflow.
Source actor index. The roster scan and the ball launch solver save it while their inner calculations use X and Y.
Current comparison slot saved by the roster scan, which restores it after calling the heading resolver.
Unadjusted distance of the roster scan's best candidate. The ball variation code later uses the same byte for its perturbation magnitude.
Best adjusted target rank so far. The candidate scan replaces it only when the new adjusted rank is smaller.
Index of the winning target candidate. The scan starts it at $FF and publishes it to $62.
Temporary candidate heading in the roster scan. The ball solver reuses it as the fractional part of the X component and during random variation.
Adjusted candidate score in target selection. The ball solver uses this scratch byte for the integer part of its X component.
Low byte of the height step in the ball-launch adjustment. The solver also uses it as the first low-byte scale operand.
High byte of the launch height step. It follows the carry from the low byte when scaling the step.
Low byte of the solver's remaining horizontal distance estimate. The target projection loop subtracts six from it each iteration.
High byte of the solver distance countdown. The old disk loader also reads the system device number from this address.
Low working byte of the ball's X difference multiplied by eight at $63E8. Other launch paths reuse it to hold the low vertical-velocity bias.
High working byte paired with $BB. The solver rotates into it while multiplying the X difference.
Low working byte of the eightfold depth difference. The projection paths also use it for the sign extension of target depth velocity.
Sign and high working byte of the eightfold depth difference, combined with the high part of its doubled copy.
Low byte of the doubled copy of the horizontal target difference. In the projected height loop it instead holds fractional vertical velocity.
High byte of the doubled horizontal difference. The height projection reuses it for integer vertical velocity.
Low byte of the second copy of the depth difference and scratch fraction for projected height.
High byte of the second copy of the depth difference. In the height prediction it carries the integer height, clamped to zero if it becomes negative.
Fractional scratch result for the ball solver's depth component, which is doubled before comparing the component magnitudes.
High byte of the depth component's two-byte scratch word. The solver normalizes or shifts it with $C3.
Candidate slot cursor for the computer target search. The loop starts at six and uses it to recover the candidate after direction projection.
Low byte of the slot's overlay catalogue pointer, selected from $7002 before the compositor indexes the per-pose records.
High byte paired with $CA. The second catalogue pointer load at $2CF8 obtains it.
Low byte of the selected overlay record pointer. The header reader uses it to fetch placement and length.
High byte of the selected overlay record pointer. It can advance after the two header bytes.
Low byte of the shared base pose pointer. $2D30 reads the first byte through this pointer.
High byte of the shared base pose pointer. Source operand setup subtracts any borrow from adjusting the low byte.
Low byte of the selected sprite destination. It is adjusted at a slot boundary while the overlay is merged.
High byte of the sprite destination. Both sprite compositor paths save the selected destination page here.
Base pose start index read from the first record header byte. The copy loop uses it to start at the occupied part of the sprite.
Two-byte base record header length used as the source adjustment.
Second base header byte. The compositor adds its placement adjustment to the overlay header offset.
Adjusted overlay placement offset. It helps compute the indexed overlay source and the backward copy's stopping point.
Overlay payload length from the second header byte, used to find the last occupied row.
Active pose or compositor slot. The compositor walks this index downward and the pose handlers keep it while using Y for other lookups.
Copy span from the base record start to the end of the overlay. The overlay loop adds it to the starting index before walking backward.
Adjusted overlay source pointer low byte. The normal and mirrored compositors both read through this pair.
Adjusted overlay source pointer high byte, after the carry or borrow from the placement adjustment.
Temporary mapped overlay byte. It is combined with base pixels preserved through the transparency mask.
Lowest depth seen while choosing the next unassigned sprite slot for the raster queue.
Sprite slot paired with the smallest depth at $DC in the ordering pass.
Current raster queue index. The interrupt at $56F8 loads it before taking a scheduled line and an operation.
Index into the occupancy queues. $58B3 saves the descending queue position before the sprite table reads reuse Y.
Number of prepared raster queue requests. The scheduler stops spanning additional interrupts when that queue length no longer calls for them.
Raster-frame counter incremented at $57AC. The low bit alternates the sprite queue work with the initialization path.
Active actor slot during motion integration and contact checks. The collision dispatcher reloads it before invoking an actor handler.
Low byte of the signed shift operand. The damping routine fills it from the fractional velocity before rotating it.
High byte of the signed shift operand. Its sign patches the OR operand at $25AB and its shifted value is written back at $25B1.
Low address of the zero-terminated score-panel string provided in X.
High address of the score-panel string provided in Y, paired with $E5.
Ink for the score-panel text and digits. The printer writes it to colour RAM for each emitted cell.
Temporary low packed digits for the score printer at $152C.
Temporary hundreds digit for the score printer. A zero suppresses the leading position unless a subsequent digit needs it.
Match target's packed ones and tens. The prompt changes it by two with decimal arithmetic.
Match target's hundreds digit. The target prompt stops increasing after this byte becomes nonzero.
Loose-ball counter inhibit flag. Setup sets it and the target-score path clears it before play.
Sign-clear side's controller choice index, used to read both input settings tables at $0F07 and $0F0D.
Sign-set side's controller choice index for the same two setup tables.
Difficulty-derived index from $139C. Computer counter and decision paths use it to choose oscillator thresholds.
Runtime flag tested by the controller setup, computer threshold selection and rematch prompt. It starts clear in the normal match setup.
Saved VIC control byte in the retained overlay blanking routine. During match setup the byte instead selects the input initializer.
Saved low nibble of the CIA2 port A reading from the retained overlay display code.
Saved sprite enable register value in the retained overlay display setup.
CPU port value saved by the retained overlay display setup before selecting $25.
Low byte of the parked-page exchange pointer. The swap indexes it by Y from zero to 255 each page.
High byte of the parked source page for the exchange. $FFE1 stops the loop when it reaches $D7.
Low byte of the low-memory page exchange pointer. The old serial page-read helper also uses this address pair as its destination.
High byte of the low-memory source page in the exchange. It starts at eight and advances at the same time as $FD.
Current pose state for each actor. The loop at $1456 reads the active slot into $8D and the dispatcher at $5B94 uses the state to choose a handler.
Fractional X position for ball and actor slots. The ball integrator at $3C26 adds the low X velocity byte here and passes carry to the integer position.
Low integer X byte for slot zero, the ball. The camera routine at $3400 uses it with the high byte at $0219.
Slot one's X low integer byte. On restart the paired stores at $1BFD and $1C02 assign $4E and $5A to slots one and two in side-dependent order.
X low integer bytes from slot two onward, before the two extra ball placement entries at $0217 and $0218.
Low X byte for the first basket-side placement. The contact handler transfers it to the ball's X coordinate at $3FC9.
Low X byte for the second basket-side placement. The contact handler selects it at $3FDA when the basket side flag is set.
High byte of integer X. The ball integrator adds the velocity sign and the carry from the low integer byte. The court camera reads slot zero at $3400.
High X byte of the first basket-side placement, paired with $0217 and transferred at $3FCF.
High X byte of the second basket-side placement. The side-specific contact path reads it from $3FE1.
Fractional depth position. The slot-zero update at $3C40 adds the low depth velocity byte at $0254 before updating $022B with carry.
Integer depth of the ball. The integrator at $3C49 adds its integer velocity and carry from the fractional update.
Integer depth of player slots one through six. The pointer queue reads these values as part of the actor's position before the screen conversion.
Depth threshold used before lower-boundary handling. Initialized from the court setup accumulator and compared with ball depth at $55E1.
Companion depth threshold byte. Setup stores the same accumulator to both $0232 and $0233.
Fractional height. The ball update at $3C53 adds the low vertical velocity byte here before adding the high velocity byte and carry to $023D.
Height of the ball. The contact handler and the height-floor test compare or update this integer byte.
First player height after the ball's height byte. The raster queue subtracts indexed player height from depth and the restart bounce uses it as one of its height references.
Player heights from slot two onward. The restart phase uses the slot-two height to form the second reach threshold at $1B53.
Low byte of horizontal velocity for each slot. It adds to the fractional X byte and can carry into the integer coordinate.
High byte of horizontal velocity. The integrator adds it with the low-byte carry to the low integer X coordinate.
Low byte of depth velocity for each slot. The stores at $6557 and $6590 respectively clear it and copy it from a player into the ball slot.
High byte of depth velocity. The ball integrator adds it to $022B after adding the velocity's low byte to $0222.
Fractional vertical velocity of the ball. $3C53 adds it to the fractional height and sends carry to the integer height calculation.
Fractional vertical velocity of actor slots one through six, added to the height fraction during motion updates.
Integer vertical velocity of the ball. Signed damping at $24DF changes it together with the fraction in $0262.
Integer vertical velocity for actor slots one through six. $664E installs it from the selected launch velocity word.
Low byte of each slot's moving-pose clock. The animation handlers add $55 and use its carry to advance the frame.
Frame portion of the moving-pose clock. On reaching six it wraps to zero, then the pose selector uses frame plus eight.
Eight-way heading kept for each slot. The placement dispatcher reads the selected actor's heading into X before applying the signed position offsets.
Base of the secondary facing group. The pose selector normally copies the primary facing here, and can preserve it according to the table at $2C24.
KERNAL screen page during selection restoration, set to four by $0E65. The address also falls inside the match's secondary facing array.
Seven slot bytes read into $89 by $1447 and copied unchanged back to the same slot at $1474. The actor update has no other reference to $89.
Saved input byte for each slot. The update loop reads it into $8B and copies the updated value back from the same temporary.
Flag bytes with the actor's side in bit seven. The restart handlers set bit six while moving assigned actors into position.
Extra sign-set flag byte written by the match setup at $1368, following the seven regular slot flags.
Extra zero flag byte initialized by the next setup store at $136D.
Half of the camera-relative horizontal position in the normal on-screen path. $4AFB rotates the low byte with carry from its high byte. $4B0D stores $FF when the right-bound test clips it.
Low integer byte of the difference between actor X and camera origin. The updater at $4AEC writes it before calculating the paired high byte at $02B8.
High bytes of the camera-relative X difference. $4AF7 stores the high byte after subtracting the camera origin, and $4B04 uses it to test the right edge.
Coarse target column for scripted actor movement. The restart setup sets it and the steering routine reads it into $90 at $1E2F.
Coarse target row paired with the columns at $02CD. $1E31 reads it and $1E34 sets the steering target Y.
Scripted movement flags. The sign bit is set while the reset target is pending. Arrival increments the byte and group progress tests bit zero through the roster.
Heading to apply when scripted steering reaches its target. The arrival path writes it into $88 when the stored heading is nonnegative.
Distance measure for the current target in each actor slot. The ranking loop at $3B12 saves the distance for each slot here before comparing actors by side.
Contact-free position recovery marker written for a slot by $4A7F. The later movement paths clear or test this byte.
Start of the per-slot movement activity flags. The pose handlers select an animated frame when the current slot's byte is nonzero.
Low part of page three. Match initialization stages part of its character output here, and the disk overlay saves and restores this page around its loads.
Timers used by pose handlers, one entry per slot. Match setup clears them and individual handlers set or decrement the counter for their action.
Seven slot bytes cleared at $1206 in the initial actor-state loop. They occupy the space before the next cleared timer field at $0313.
Slot-zero byte of the pose timer field cleared by match setup. The restart path at $3A66 writes four when selecting its actor.
Continuation of the per-player pose timer field during the match. The return-to-selection vector restore reuses these addresses for the saved KERNAL vectors.
Candidate overlay pose index. The heading-group lookup first writes its base, and the adjustment path adds a pose offset or replaces it with an absolute index.
Overlay pose index for player slots one through six, following the slot-zero entry. $2CFF uses the selected index to look up a record in that slot's catalogue.
Candidate base-pose selector. $61B6 writes the heading base plus the current pose selector, then $624E compares it with the slot's saved value.
Base-pose selector for player slots one through six. The compositor loads the selected byte and doubles it to address the shared base record table.
Candidate base-pose mirror flag. $6198 clears it before the heading check and $61A9 sets it when the primary heading uses a mirrored row.
Saved mirror flags for the base-pose slot selectors. $2D64 tests the flag before choosing between direct copy and horizontal mirror.
Candidate overlay mirror flag at selector setup and an indexed flag base for the compositor. The path at $61CD clears its initial one for mirrored secondary headings.
First byte of the reload stub's destination. $0E31 fills the buffer from $0E76 before $0E37 jumps here. The match hand-over has the same leading two bytes as the pre-load RAM.
Two side-indexed contact flags. The oscillator paths at $4CAD and $4CBE assign zero or $80. Both bytes belong to the reload destination when the match ends.
Temporary X coordinate for $6690 or $669B. The three shifts at $66A0 reduce it to a column. The opposing-side path mirrors it around column $53.
Two side-indexed button hold counters. $224F increments the selected byte and a count of three switches the controlled actor. The clear path at $2269 resets it on release.
Workspace cleared by match setup at $1295 and the restart path at $19E4. The return stub overwrites it along with the rest of its destination.
Returns immediately. The following two bytes still hold the little-endian address $080F.
Address $080F remains in the two bytes after the return at $0800.
Jumps to $080D. The exposed transition code calls this vector with the file selector in X.
Returns immediately. The following two bytes still hold the receive routine address $08C9.
Address $08C9 remains after the return at $0806.
Returns immediately. The following two bytes still hold the send routine address $08DF.
Address $08DF remains after the return at $0809.
Returns before the independent file-loader entry at $080D.

Saves the numeric file selector from X. Adds $40 to make the PETSCII name, exposes the KERNAL, sets a one-character name and calls LOAD for device 8 with secondary address 2. Restores banking on return.
Isolated byte $23 after the KERNAL load wrapper's return at $083B. The next entry starts at $083D by loading $FF.
Loads $FF before falling into the serial exchange. The calls at $08CA, $08D0, $08E0 and $08E6 enter directly at $083F and pass the outgoing byte in A.
Exchanges eight bits through CIA2 port A, clocking at $0856 and $0876 and shifting the received bits into $0961. Returns the result in A.
Samples $D012 until it changes. Takes another sample when the original value minus the new one is negative, and returns after the other transition.

Adds $40 to the byte at $096C, selects secondary address eight on the device in $BA, and requests a one-byte filename at $096C before calling KERNAL LOAD. This preserved path jumps into the fragment at $08F8. The match's numbered file requests enter instead at $080D.
Stores A through $FE/$FF with I/O hidden by $24, restores I/O with $25, advances Y and increments the pointer high byte on Y wrap. The branches return to $08A6 inside the retained load path.
Sends X and Y with bit seven set in the second byte, then receives a 256-byte page into the buffer at $FE/$FF. The final serial response returns its high bit in carry.
Sends X and Y with bits six and seven set in the second byte, then transmits a 256-byte page from the buffer at $FE/$FF. The final serial response returns its high bit in carry.
Loads a repeat count of two, samples $D012 and compares that sample with another read. The low-page restore routine begins at $0900, immediately after this fragment.
The loader copies the saved $0D00 page back to $0300 before its first file request.
Copies zero page to $0B00, page two to $0C00 and page three to $0D00. This code runs in the disk overlay when the menu switches to the match.
Saves page three into $0D00. X wraps after the last store at $0DFF, then the overlay save returns.
Byte $F4 immediately after the return at $092D and before the indexed store at $092F. File M supplies it in the overlay page exchanged into $0900.
Stores A at $0962,X and counts X down. The backward branch now reaches the return at $092D. The display-blanking code begins at $0935.

Saves the banking port in $F8, synchronises to the raster, masks the display control at $D011, saves the low nibble of CIA2 port A and saves and clears sprite enable at $D015. The preserved tail pulls one stack byte before returning.
Eight-bit serial exchange workspace. $083F seeds it with the outgoing byte, $0860 rotates incoming bits into it and $087C returns the accumulated byte.
Legacy storage base for the indexed store at $092F. The ten bytes through $096B retain instruction-like overlay bytes. The one-byte filename follows them at $096C.
One-byte filename buffer addressed by the legacy LOAD sequence at $088B. That sequence adds $40 to the byte and passes its address with length one to KERNAL SETNAM.
The one-byte filename passed to KERNAL SETNAM by the file loader at $080D. That routine adds $40 to the incoming selector before storing the letter here.
The bytes at $0A01–$0A3F duplicate the menu font at $0A32–$0A70. This copy starts at row four (zero-based) of glyph $22 and continues up to the retained rows at $0A40.

Preserved menu font bytes matching $0A71–$0B1C of the selection program. The first byte is row three (zero-based) of glyph $2A in the eight-byte set at $091E. The block appears at this address after $FFCE exchanges the parked disk overlay into low RAM.
Three $EA bytes precede the disk loader's entry at $0E03.
The loader enters here after loading B. The trampoline jumps to match initialization at $0EBE.
Banks in KERNAL and copies the zero-page and work-area images from $0B00-$0DFF back into $0000 and $0200-$03FF. Copies the reload stub from $0E76 to $0334 and executes it there.

Six stored bytes between the unconditional jump to the copied reload stub and the separate page-save entry. The byte pattern starts with TAY and STA $0300,Y and ends in a partial indexed store; the jump skips this fragment.
Copies $0000, $0200 and $0300 into the three saved workspace pages at $0B00 through $0DFF.
Isolated $02 after the page-save return and before the screen and vector restore entry.
Sets the KERNAL screen page to $04, copies 32 bytes from $FD30 to $0314 and jumps to the RAM overlay entry at $FF80.
Copied to $0334 before execution. Blanks the screen, sets up device 8 with secondary address 1 and the 16-byte name at $0366, calls the KERNAL loader, then enters $0810.

Eight bytes copied after the jump at the end of the return stub. They contain a space, DOS, two asterisks and two zero bytes. The observed SETNAM call starts eight bytes later at the wildcard filename.
Sixteen bytes copied to $0366 with the return-to-menu stub and passed to SETNAM before LOAD.
Six bytes after the 16-byte reload name. Decoded on their own they pull A, store it at $DC00, pull A again and execute RTI. The reload copy carries them along after its filename.
Masks CPU interrupts, banks out the KERNAL, blanks the screen, disables CIA1 timer interrupts and selects the VIC's $C000 bank before setting up the match vectors.
Seven initial flag bytes for the match slots, including zero for the ball. The six nonzero entries alternate $40 and $C0 so the two sides can be distinguished by the sign bit.
Six settings indexed by either side's controller choice. The setup at $1257 and $1263 writes the values into $54 and $55.
Six secondary input settings read alongside the primary indices during a normal start and written into $56 and $57.
Points the hardware IRQ at $575B and NMI at $0E85, then clears match flags, stages glyphs from character ROM and prepares the bottom line of text.

Tests $0342. With the flag clear it pulls A and returns from the interrupt. With the flag set it enables interrupts, clears decimal mode, disables VIC interrupts, clears four SID frequency registers and calls $6936 before falling into match setup.

Clears four workspace pages at $0200–$05FF, fills the range starting at $040B with $FF and calls $327D. Clears actor and scroll state, copies the sprite template at $6950 to $F400 and clears the per-slot work arrays for seven slots.
Reads six draft slots using the index table at $1396 and stores their zero-based indices in $0769–$076E.
Sets camera X to $00A8 and the cached tile column to $14, clears the fine-scroll state and configures the draw pointers for the first view of the court.

Writes the left 20 cells of each of 24 rows from $E014 to the screen at $CC00. Copies all 40 colour bytes of each row from the matching viewport at $E814 to colour RAM, advancing the source by 80 columns per row.
Copies 20 cells per row from $E400 to the right half of the screen at $CC14, completing the initial 24-row viewport.
Calls the video setup, enables multicolour sprites and clears sprite expansion. Copies each slot's initial flag byte from $0F00 and seeds its X position, Y byte and per-slot state.

Maps option $FF26 through $139C when $FF23 is set, calls $1D12 for option index two, seeds $08/$09 with slots three and four and sets sprite multicolour zero. Uses $F5 to select fixed colour values or a pair of entries from $0F07/$0F0D for each side.
Copies the three palette bytes at $EFFD-$EFFF into the VIC registers $D021-$D023.
Six offsets into the saved draft at $FF1D. The loop at $10F4 uses the offsets to reorder the picks and subtracts one from each character number.
Three values selected by the difficulty byte at $FF26. The third value shares $139E with the independent indexed reader at $5560.
Third difficulty value for the read at $1220. The restart code separately reads this address at $5560 and doubles the result.
Ten roster indices into the first group of speed words at $20DE. $2069 looks up the entry using the actor's roster ID and doubles it to select a word.
Ten roster indices into the second group of speed words. When the active slot is the ball possessor, $205A reads the matching roster entry and adds ten before doubling it.

Ten roster parameters selecting the amount of ball velocity variation for mode zero at $5184. The loop at $51A7 adds another variation step for each increment through index nine, with zero treated as one.

Ten roster selectors into the contact threshold table at $4C83. The actor contact branch reads one at $6097 and continues toward release only when the oscillator sample is at least the selected threshold.
Ten indices into the vertical launch velocity table at $6654. $6640 reads one using the selected Y index, doubles it and copies that word to the actor velocity.
Ten roster parameters selecting ball velocity variation in mode one at $518E. The selected byte goes to the same variation loop as mode zero.

Ten roster selectors used by the lower follow-through branch at $5E54. Zero skips the random test. Other values select the threshold at $5E9D. The fallback path at $519E also uses this field for ball velocity variation.
Ten roster parameters used by the mode-two ball velocity variation branch at $5198. The follow-through branch at $5E12 also reads this selector and skips its random test when it is zero.

Iterates the ball and active players, copying each actor's position, rates and flags into zero-page workspace. Players run their control and action handlers and the ball uses its own routine. Dirty fields are copied back as the loop moves to the next actor.

Fills 40 screen cells at $F3C0 with character $38 and clears the score panel. Uses the lengths from the two team-name records to center the text. Records the two score columns in $3C and $3B before drawing the numeric fields.
Prints green and blue totals using the scores in $37-$3A and column positions at $3B-$3C.
Takes the low two BCD digits in A and the hundreds digit in X. Suppresses leading zeroes and writes the digits and their colour starting at column Y.
Draws both scores with the alternate decimal printer, whose temporary digit and colour fields live at $15C8-$15CA.
Takes the leading digit in X, the other two packed in A and the starting column in Y. Suppresses leading zeroes, writes each displayed digit and its colour, and ends with two $0A tiles.
Temporary packed decimal low digits in the score printer at $1584.
Temporary hundreds digit saved from X by the alternate score printer.
Colour byte used by the alternate score printer. The caller sets five for green and $0E for blue.
Draws the target prompt and current BCD value. Polls the applicable controller and debounces the choice using the raster countdown at $07AB.
Polls input at $17BB. The confirmation bit branches to $166A. The direction test chooses the increase path or checks the low target byte against three before allowing a decrement.
Uses decimal mode to subtract two from the two-byte value at $EA-$EB, then redraws the target. The preceding guard keeps the 2-point minimum.
Uses decimal mode to add two to $EA-$EB. The caller only reaches this branch while the hundreds byte is zero.
Clears the setup prompt, displays the selected target, waits for the countdown and then enters the match loop. Compares both scores against $EA-$EB after each update.
Fire bit mask $10 used by the target and rematch input checks.
Left-direction mask $04, tested while editing the target score.
Right-direction mask $08 for increasing the displayed score target.
Reads either both joystick ports together or the selected human port, using the match options held at $FF23 and $FF1C.
Stores A in $07AB and waits for it to become negative. The raster handler decrements it.

Prints a zero-terminated string from X:Y at column A in $CFC0 and assigns each cell the colour in $E7. Maps digits to $00-$09, the space to $0A, letters to the match font and punctuation to dedicated indices.
Writes the match font's blank ($0A) across the 40-cell bottom row at $CFC0.
Fifteen-byte buffer including its terminator. Holds the converted green name for the match panel and is filled by $0FB5.
Trimmed length of the green team name. Setup writes it and the score panel and winner caption use it for centering.
Blue team panel name buffer, filled with the converted characters at $0FE9. The setup saves its trimmed length separately before adding the zero terminator.
Trimmed length of the blue team name. The panel subtracts it together with the green length to center the two names.
Zero-terminated caption printed while the target score is selected.
Zero-terminated prefix for the target-score announcement after confirmation.
Zero-terminated phrase appended to the winning team's name.
Zero-terminated question asking whether to play again with the same teams.
Zero-terminated YES choice, printed at column $22 when $07AE is nonzero.
Zero-terminated NO with one trailing space to cover the three cells used by YES.
Zero and two spaces, terminated by zero for the score panel printer.
Return instruction immediately after the initial score caption. The display interrupt calls it at $5A90 and then goes to its register restore.

Splits the low ball X byte, Y byte and height byte into pairs of hexadecimal digits. Skips the space at screen-code index ten when displaying A through F. Writes the digit pairs at columns 1–2, 4–5 and 7–8 of the score panel, with trailing spaces at columns 6 and 9.
Clears the action flags at $41-$42 and dispatches from the ball phase at $20. A zero phase returns immediately.
The phase $50 path performs the made-basket setup, calls the scoring routine at $558F and starts a ten-tick follow-up timer.

Phase $54 compares the two-byte totals at $37/$38 and $39/$3A against the two-byte target at $EA/$EB. If either meets or exceeds the target, the code sets delay $14 and phase $C0. Otherwise it proceeds to phase $55.
Phase $55 adjusts the ball's X coordinate by $14 on court zero, using the sign of $21 to choose the direction. Calls $2587 and $3AE5 to prepare the actor target before the side adjustment at $1B01.
Completes the adjustment of the actor target in X based on the sign of the byte at $21. Calls $5544 with the target Y in A, then writes the delay $28 to $23 and switches the ball phase to $14.

Dispatches phases $72 through $75 and then $90 through $92, $C0, $80 and $81. The first branch raises the ball from height $37 with vertical velocity $03E8, assigns actors 1 and 2, and starts the delay for the next phase.

When the ball's vertical velocity is negative, compares its height with the two actor heights plus $28. The branch based on those comparisons can select a new X velocity sign and set vertical velocity $0258. Otherwise the delay counts down and can set both readiness bytes at $41/$42.
Phase $74 waits for the delay at $23. Phase $75 clears bit six of each actor flag from $02A1,Y down to actor one, assigns actors 3 and 4 and returns the ball phase to zero.
Phase $90 clears the delay and both assigned actor indices, saves the actor count in $22 and increments the phase. Phase $91 delegates to $66C5.

Tests bit zero of the per-actor flags at $02DB,Y. When each actor has reached the required state, writes the ordered X values $4E and $5A to $0211/$0212 according to the side bit. If $EC is zero it switches the ball phase to $70.
For phase $C0, clears the assigned actor indices, decrements the delay and then moves the ball to X=$0154. Phases $80 and $81 delegate to $1C89 and $1C5C.
Return shared by the immediate restart flag check and the path that calls $1C5C before returning.
Low byte of the upper-boundary left X limit, paired with $1C48.
Low byte of the upper-boundary right X limit, paired with $1C49.
Low byte of the lower-boundary left X limit, paired with $1C4A.
Low byte of the lower-boundary right X limit. The restart placement handler also uses this address as the base of its indexed high-X entries.
High byte of the upper-boundary left X limit. It is also the second high-X entry of the placement lookup at $1A20.
High byte of the upper-boundary right X limit, used with $1C45 by the clamp.
High byte of the lower-boundary left X limit, used with $1C46 for both testing and assignment.
High byte of the lower-boundary right X limit. The restart placement at $1A26 also uses this address as the base for its depth values.
Counts Y down from six while loading zero, then clears the selection at $05.

ANDs bit zero across $02DB for slots one through the count in $02. If every flag is set, uses the sign of $1F to assign $4E and $5A in either order to the low X bytes of slots one and two, then sets ball phase $70.

Clears both assigned indices and the ball's horizontal velocities, then places the ball at X=$0154, Y=$8A. Marks seven actor reset entries, sets each target coordinate and facing from the tables at $1CFA–$1D05, clears the delay and advances the phase.
Same-side target columns indexed by (slot minus one) divided by two. The main restart loop visits seven slots, so its fourth index shares the first row byte at $1CFD.
Same-side target rows used at $1CCC. Slot seven shares the first opposite-side column byte at $1D00 as its row value.
Target columns subtracted from $53 for actors on the opposite side. In the seven-slot setup the fourth index shares the first opposite-side row byte at $1D03.
The opposite-side row lookup starts here and also reads $1D06 for slot seven. The script at $6703 uses this same base for its six-player setup.
Fourth row value for the indexed read at $1CD9. The seven-slot loop reaches it with X equal to three.
Eleven small positive values after the last known opposite-side row. The slot loop ends at index three, so its row lookup stops at the preceding byte at $1D06.
Visits slots six through one. For each actor with the sign bit set at $02A1, uses its roster index at $0768 and maps seven fields through $1D67. The final two fields keep zero as a sentinel.
Ten replacement indices used for the sign-set side by $1D12. Inputs zero through nine map to 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 8, 9 and 9.

Takes the active actor from $0E. Its side bit and the assigned actor indices at $08/$09 choose an input byte from $54–$57, saved in $8B. The actor's state then selects the human handlers, the ball-directed heading calculation, a computer decision, or an early return.

For each of the 24 fine bearings, one selects the rounded heading at $1E73 and zero retains the current heading at $1E7E. The routine consults this table after checking that the rounded heading differs by at most one without crossing the wrap.

Handles the pending turn bit in $02A1,Y with an oscillator-selected heading. The regular path gets coarse target coordinates from $21ED, adjusts the target for the side and ball phase, clamps the horizontal coordinate with $C550/$C551, and translates the heading from $25B4 into the eight-direction command used at $2013.
Eight signed horizontal offsets. $1F08 adds the selected offset to $8E before the court-range clamp.
Adds $0A to $8E when the signs of $1F and $06 match, or subtracts $0A when they differ, and jumps to the clamp at $1F0D.

Selects reference slot seven or eight from the sign of $1F XOR $06 and gets a heading and distance from $226D. At distance ten or greater sends that heading to $2013. The near path at $1FA8 tests $1E before continuing.
Compares the actor flags at $02A1,Y with $1F. Different sign bits choose heading six at $1F9E. Matching sign bits choose heading two at $1FA3.
Compares $02A1,Y with $1F using the opposite heading choice to $1F8E. Different sign bits choose two and matching sign bits choose six.
Tests $1E against $E0 in the close-reference case. At or above that threshold jumps to $1FFB, which checks whether to clear horizontal movement.
Immediate operand $E0 in the phase comparison at $1FAA. At or above this cutoff the code jumps to $1FFB, otherwise it tests the controlled slots at $1FB1.
Chooses a CIA port from the side assignment at $FF1C. Uses the CPU controller when the side flag at $3D is set, otherwise passes the direction bits to the movement decoder.
Uses the opposite port mapping from green and checks $3E before choosing human movement or the CPU controller.
Masks off the fire bit and maps the four direction bits through $2106. Invalid entries take the stationary path.

Uses the direction-table byte at $2116,X to transform the 16-bit value at $27/$28 into $0A/$0B. Zero clears the result, bit zero subtracts one quarter of the magnitude, and bit seven negates the result.

Twenty little-endian magnitudes read into $27/$28 before the direction scaler at $2098. The movement path at $206E selects the index through roster settings and uses index five when $20 is at least $90. The path at $5565 selects the index from the actor field at $139E.
High-byte base of the actor speed words. The readers at $2073 and $556A use the same even index as the corresponding low-byte reads.
Sixteen entries indexed by the low joystick nibble at $1FF6. Nonnegative entries go to the heading update at $2013. A negative entry follows the path that can clear the actor's horizontal velocity.
Sixteen direction entries for $2098. Zero suppresses an X component, bit zero requests scaling to three quarters, and bit seven makes it negative.

Low byte of ball X velocity in the first of eight four-byte heading records. The contact path at $60B5 multiplies the actor heading by four and copies the record to the ball's horizontal velocity fields.
High byte of ball X velocity in each four-byte heading record. The contact path loads it with the same index as the low byte.
Low byte of ball Y velocity in each four-byte heading record. The contact path loads it with the same index as the X components.
High byte of ball Y velocity in each four-byte heading record. Loaded at $60CD and stored at $025B.
Runs the teammate selector for both sides, updating $08 from its first returned Y and $09 from the second.

Saves the current actor Y in $36. With ball phase zero, returns the possessor when it is on the same side. Otherwise it checks the current actor's camera-relative X. Outside the central band, and while ball phase is below $50, it scans eligible teammates for the appropriate extreme of the column at $02AA. Returns the chosen actor in Y or the original actor if the scan supplies no selection.

Reduces actor and ball X to units of eight pixels and Y to units of four. Stores actor coordinates at $90/$91 and ball coordinates at $8E/$8F. For actors outside the two controlled slots, divides both reduced Y coordinates by four again.

For a controlled actor who lacks possession, counts fire detections in the side's $033D counter. A count of three invokes $26CB and latches the counter at $80. A released button or possession clears it.

Saves the candidate index Y while reducing the current indexed object's position to two coarse coordinates at $8E/$8F. For candidate zero it scales the signed horizontal velocities by half the current object's $02E9 value using shift-and-add, then adds the projection to the candidate position. Other candidates use their stored positions directly. It reduces the resulting coordinates into $90/$91, calls $25B4 and converts the returned heading through $2388.

Maps 24 fine bearings to eight headings. Indices 2–4 select one, 5–7 select two, and the group for zero wraps through indices 23, zero and one. The restart path at $1E66 compares this result with the actor's current heading.

Converts the positions indexed by Y and X into coarse coordinates in $9F-$A2. X uses (position + 4) divided by eight and Y uses (position + 2) divided by four, with offsets $20 and $40 respectively. Calls $23FC and maps the returned heading through $2388 to return a direction mask in A.

Computes the unsigned magnitudes and signs of the two coordinate differences. Orders the magnitudes, approximates their ratio with four trial additions and reduces the result to one of four steps. The signs and the larger axis select a sector, and $18 wraps to zero. Returns the heading in A and $AD and the distance estimate in X.
Buckets the trial sum in $AB at thresholds 2, 6 and 12. Replaces $AB with the resulting step from zero through three.
Subtracts the coordinate at $9F,X from $A1,X. Writes the magnitude to $A3,X and a sign marker of $80 for a negative difference or zero otherwise to $A5,X.
Starts with the larger magnitude at $A9. If neither addition overflows, computes three quarters of the sum using two right shifts. Replaces the initial distance only when that result is smaller.

Subtracts one arithmetic eighth from each signed ball velocity word. When the vertical high position is zero and the damped vertical velocity high byte is $FF or $00, clears vertical velocity and the low position byte, then uses the SID oscillator's low three bits to decide whether to skip the horizontal updates. The two horizontal words are zeroed if their shifted values are zero.
Copies ball X divided by eight to $1A and ball Y divided by four to $1D.
Copies the sign bit from $E4 into the immediate operand at $25AB. Rotates $E3 after each sign-extended high-byte shift. The loop runs X plus one times for the callers' nonnegative counts.
The immediate operand patched by $25A4 to $00 or $80. After each logical right shift, the OR instruction restores the sign bit before rotating the low byte at $E3.

Computes signed differences for coarse coordinates $90/$91 relative to $8E/$8F. Orders the magnitudes, divides to approximate their ratio, then uses that ratio and the signs to select a heading from 0 through 23 in A and $9C. Returns the distance estimate from $9D in X.
Converts the ratio accumulator in $9A to a step of zero through three at thresholds 2, 6 and 12.
Compares destination $90,X with origin $8E,X. Stores their unsigned absolute difference in $92,X and writes $80 to $94,X for a negative difference, or zero otherwise.
Starts with the larger magnitude at $98. If neither addition overflows, computes three quarters of the sum and keeps it when it is smaller. Writes the result at $9D.

Returns in X the larger of absolute Y displacement from $7D and halved horizontal displacement from $7A/$7B, with a $FF result when the unhalved difference spans too many pages. On the negative one-page branch it complements the low difference before shifting, so negative and positive distances can round differently. Uses actor slot Y and clobbers $0C.

Scans the six actor slots in cyclic order after the current actor. Selects a same-side slot whose $02AA entry is not $FF and whose side flags have bit six clear. Stores the selection in the side's controlled slot and, when its pose state is zero, sets its pose flag and timer to ten.
Writes phase six to $6C to start the triangle effect at its next dispatch.
Writes phase thirteen to $6D to start the three-tick noise onset at $2AAF.
Dispatches through a jump table selected by $6C. The handler updates SID voice 1 for a sound effect.
Low byte of the jump target written at $2715 immediately before dispatch.
High byte of the jump target written at $271B immediately before dispatch.
Eleven pointers to SID voice 1 effect steps, including the idle RTS.
High-byte base for the voice 1 phase table. The load at $2718 uses the same even offset as the low-byte read.
Clears the gate, sets envelope and starting frequency, then sets gate and noise together and initializes the first sweep countdown.
Adds the signed step $FF88 to the voice 1 frequency, decrements the countdown at $76 and advances the effect after it expires.
Subtracts $00F0 from the voice 1 frequency and writes the two bytes to the SID. When $76 runs down, sets it to one and advances $6C.
Subtracts six from the voice 1 frequency. At countdown expiry switches the noise gate off, sets the next countdown to one and advances $6C.
Subtracts one from the voice 1 frequency. At countdown expiry clears both SID frequency bytes and returns $6C to the idle phase.

Clears the gate with triangle selected, sets attack and decay to $05 and sustain and release to $16, writes starting frequency $0960 and enables the gate. Sets the phase countdown to three and advances $6C.
Subtracts $0032 from the voice 1 frequency and writes both bytes to SID. On countdown expiry sets $76 to two and advances $6C.
Subtracts $0032 from the voice 1 frequency. On countdown expiry sets $76 to three and advances $6C.
Subtracts $0032 from the voice 1 frequency. When the countdown expires, clears the triangle gate and starts the final twelve-tick countdown.
Runs the triangle release tail by decreasing pitch one unit per tick. On tick expiration writes zero to both voice 1 frequency registers and the phase selector at $6C.
Doubles $6D to select the phase address from $289E and jumps through the patched operand at $289C.
Low byte of the voice 2 jump target installed by $2892.
High byte of the voice 2 jump target installed by $2898.
Eighteen little-endian jump targets indexed by twice $6D. The dispatcher at $288B copies the selected target into the jump operand at $289C.
High-byte base for the voice 2 phase dispatch. The load at $2895 uses the same even index as the low-byte load at $288F.
Returns without changing the SID when phase $6D is zero.
Sets up SID voice 2 with noise, envelope and sweep state and advances $6D.
Calls the shared frequency integrator, adds $003C to its step at $72/$73 and advances the phase with an eleven-tick countdown when $77 expires.
Integrates the current frequency step, then subtracts $2625 from it. At expiration clears the noise gate and starts a nine-tick tail.
Integrates the step and subtracts $2625 from it during the nine-tick release. At expiration clears selection at $6D and both voice 2 frequency bytes.
Sets the noise envelope to $54/$00, base frequency to $08FC, accumulated offset to zero and step to $FF4C. Starts the gate and sets a thirty-tick countdown.
Integrates the current step and subtracts five from it each tick. After thirty ticks writes $10 to the voice control and clears its frequency and phase.
Sets the triangle envelope to $47/$00, base frequency to $0898, step and offset to zero and advances the phase with a twelve-tick countdown.
Integrates the frequency and subtracts $001C from the step each tick. When $77 expires, releases the triangle gate and starts another twelve ticks.
Continues the triangle frequency integration and decrements the step by $001C during release. When $77 expires, clears the phase and silences the frequency registers.
Selects pulse width $0200, envelope $09/$09 and base frequency $05E6. Clears step and offset, opens the gate and starts the five-tick first phase and sixty-tick outer timer.
Integrates frequency, decrements the step by one and, on countdown expiry, adds $0037 to the offset and selects the next phase for two ticks.

Decrements the outer timer and exits by silencing the voice if it expires. Otherwise integrates frequency and decrements the step. When the phase countdown reaches zero subtracts $0037 from the offset and switches back to the preceding phase for two ticks.
Writes noise envelope $04/$78 and frequency $03E8 before opening the gate and starting a three-tick countdown.
Waits for $77 to count down, then closes the noise gate and sets the next phase to five ticks.
Adds $4BF6 to the frequency on even ticks. When the five-tick countdown expires, sets the next countdown to four and advances the phase.
Subtracts $0A22 from the frequency each tick. After four ticks sets the software frequency word to $4000 for the next phase and starts a ten-tick countdown.
Adds $7777 to the frequency when the countdown is divisible by four. At expiry clears the selected phase and both voice 2 frequency bytes.
Adds the 16-bit step at $72/$73 to the accumulated offset at $74/$75. Adds that new offset to the base at $70/$71 and writes the resulting frequency to SID voice 2.
Copies the two 16-bit horizontal velocity words from actor Y to slot zero at $0246/$024D and $0254/$025B.
Copies the two vertical velocity bytes from actor slot Y to the ball in slot zero.
Reverses the nonzero headings around heading zero. The primary and secondary pose paths at $61AC and $61D0 use this table when the heading index is at least five.
Five base offsets for the roster overlay pose groups. $61E0 chooses one using the normalized secondary heading and saves it at $031A.
Five row starts separated by 23 bytes. $61E6 fetches the row, then adds the current pose selector to index the table at $2BB1.

Five 23-byte groups indexed by the heading base at $2BAC plus the pose selector at $8A. The reader at $61ED takes a high-bit entry as a complete pose index after masking the bit. Other entries are offsets that go through the adjustment logic before being added to the base at $031A.
Indexed by pose selector at $61BB. Zero updates the secondary heading at $0285 from $027E for this slot. A nonzero entry skips that update.
Base index for eight normalized headings in the sprite pose catalogue. Entries are spaced 23 apart. $61B0 loads the heading's base and adds the pose selector at $8A before storing $0321.

First of eight low bytes paired with $2C4B. Interpreted together the values run from minus four to plus eight and have their extrema at indices six and two. The adjacent active placement tables use the same eight-heading layout.
Eight sign bytes for the retained offsets starting at $2C43. The last three entries are $FF, corresponding to the three negative low-byte offsets.
Eight signed bytes after the paired offsets at $2C43 and $2C4B. They alternate in groups between minus one and plus one. No reader was found during the match watch window.
Two positive bytes, $1E and $23, between the retained depth offset row and the first active ball placement offsets at $2C5D.
Low bytes of eight X offsets added to the ball carrier's position by $64A7. The paired high bytes begin at $2C65.
High bytes of eight signed X offsets for $64AF. Added with carry from the low-byte addition at $64A7.
Signed Y offset by heading for placement at $64BA. Added to the carrier's Y coordinate to position the ball.
Low bytes of eight heading-dependent X offsets used by $6510 with the raised placement height.
High bytes paired with $2C76. The X placement carries from the low-byte add into these signed high bytes.
Eight signed Y offsets added to the actor's Y coordinate after the raised placement at $64FD adds $1C to the actor's height.
Low bytes of eight heading-dependent X offsets used by both flat placement handlers. The jump at $6443 supplies the heading index.
High bytes paired with the flat placement X offsets. Both handlers add these with the carry from the low-byte addition.
Eight signed depth offsets paired with the flat placement X offsets. $6549 and $657B add them to the actor's depth before storing the ball position.

Runs while $076F is clear. Counts unpossessed updates in $C559 if phase is not $C1 and $EC is clear. The counter wrapping selects phase $80. On the first call with $0786 clear, sets it and begins refreshing the actor poses. Later calls increment $0787 for phases below $C0.

Uses the active slot in X to find a character-specific pointer table at $7002. Selects an overlay record by $031B,X and an underlying pose record by $0322,X, then reads their two-byte placement headers.
Uses the slot and buffer selector at $0771 to patch the copy destinations from $3159, then copies the base-pose bytes in two spans separated by the VIC sprite padding byte.
Low byte of the patched base-pose source at $2D92. The header adjustment at $2D57 selects where the copy starts.
High byte of the adjusted base-pose source at $2D92. It includes the borrow from subtracting the starting offset from the low byte.
Low destination byte of the base-pose store at $2D95. The selected sprite buffer pointer provides this byte.
High destination byte of the base-pose store at $2D95. The copy advances Y until the current sprite span limit.
Patchable loop limit for the base sprite copy. When the current limit is $3F, $2DA4 changes it to $7F for the continuation. The copy tail then selects the overlay path or jumps to $3228.
Patches the three source and destination byte columns of the recolour loop. Uses the selected overlay pointer and adjusted placement offset to align the overlay with the base pose.
Remaps each of three overlay bytes through $0568, keeps base pixels selected by the masks derived through $0668, then combines the remapped overlay and the preserved pixels.
Remaps and writes the portions of the overlay above the base-pose start. Steps backward by three bytes per row.
Low source operand of the first extension-column read at $2E6C.
High source operand of the first extension fetch. The next load maps the byte through the lookup table at $0568.
Low destination operand of the store at $2E72 for the first extension column.
High destination operand of the first extension store. The second column fetch starts immediately after it.
Low source operand of the second extension-column load at $2E75.
High source operand of the second extension fetch. Its byte is remapped through $0568 before writing the second column.
Low destination operand of the store at $2E7B for the second extension column.
High destination operand of the store at $2E7B. The adjacent instruction reads the remaining extension column.
Low source operand of the third extension-column load at $2E7E.
High source operand of the third extension fetch, followed by the final lookup through $0568 for this row.
Low destination operand of the third extension store. Its high byte follows at $2E86.
High byte of the patched destination operand for the third pixel byte in the extension row. $2E84 stores the mirrored result here plus Y.
Writes zeroes backward from the top edge of the composite shape before proceeding to the next slot.
Low destination operand for clearing undrawn space above the sprite shape. Both compositor paths patch this byte.
Patched destination high byte of the clear loop's store at $2E96. The normal and mirrored sprite setup paths set it before the loop clears bytes above the shape.

When $077F is set, copies eleven rows for each of two sprite shapes to the corresponding alternate-buffer images for the first slot. Exchanges the buffer selector between 0 and 6 and clears the request.
Low byte of the first of twelve interleaved destination pointers for two sets of six sprite composites. The pointer index is twice the sum of the active slot and its buffer selector.
High byte of the first destination pointer, paired with $3159. The compositor reads both with the same even offset and patches the ordinary or mirrored copy loop.
Initial pointer values for the first sprite buffer. $5A38 adds the actor index and writes the resulting pointer into both screen matrices for the assigned hardware sprite.
Pointer values read at $5922 for the later of two raster events. The queue stores the chosen pointer at $03F3,X for the IRQ.
Pointer values read at $58EA for the earlier raster event, scheduled ten lines after the object's Y.
Initial pointers for the second sprite buffer, used by $5A50 instead of the first buffer when the buffer branch selects this set.
Second-buffer pointers used for the event scheduled 21 lines after the object's Y. The IRQ gets the selected byte through $03F3.
The first seven bytes are the second-buffer pointer strip indexed by the queue's earlier raster event at $5902.
Five values spaced six apart, from zero to 24, between the last sprite queue pointer row and the mirror routine. They are past the bounded pointer lookup at $5902.

Patches the three source columns of the base record and the three destination columns of the selected sprite slot. Maps each byte through the multicolour mirror table at $0568 and reverses the byte-column order. At the first slot boundary it skips one padding byte and continues into the next slot span.
Low operand of the first base-pose source for mirroring. The setup at $319C also uses it to compute the other two source columns.
High byte of the first mirror source. Each fetched byte is mapped through the two-bit-group reversal table before storing.
Low destination operand for the first mirror source, offset two bytes from the sprite row base.
High destination operand of the mirror store at $31F8. Its destination is the sprite row's last column.
Low source operand of the middle-column mirror load. The setup at $319C adds one to the first source.
High source operand of the middle-column mirror load. $31A8 propagates carry from the increment of its low byte.
Low destination operand of the middle-column mirror store. It is one greater than the selected sprite pointer's low byte.
High destination operand of the middle-column mirror store. It shares the page selected at $31DA with the other columns.
Low operand of the third mirrored source load, computed two bytes from the first source.
High operand of the third mirrored source load, including carry from adding two to the source low byte.
Low operand of the final store in the mirror loop. This column uses the unmodified sprite buffer base low byte.
High operand of the final store in the mirror loop. The following increments advance Y by one complete three-byte row.
Immediate operand of the CPY at $3210. The mirror loop patches it first to $3F and then to $7F to skip the padding between the adjoining sprite buffers.

Saves slot and adjusted overlay pointers. Blends the overlay backwards from its end through the transparency mask table $0668, adjusting the slot base at the padding boundary, then copies the remaining overlay bytes before entering the common compositor tail.
Low operand of the retained overlay source. $3237 saves the adjusted low byte both here and in the indirect pointer at $D9.
High operand of the retained overlay source, after subtracting any borrow from the initial Y adjustment.
Low destination byte of the mirrored overlay tail loop. $322A patches it with the selected sprite slot's low byte.
High byte of the store operand at $3272, copied from $D1. The loop copies the remaining mirrored overlay bytes to that sprite destination before joining the common compositor tail.

Enumerates all 256 input bytes. At $0568 stores each byte with its four two-bit pixel groups reversed. At $0668 stores a mask with both bits set for each zero pixel group so that an overlay pixel of colour zero preserves the underlying sprite.

A 16-byte block between the table-building return and the template refresh. Its first nine bytes are zero. The remaining values are multiples of three through twelve, unlike the surrounding executable code.

Compares template index $0789 and the high byte of camera X plus $80 with their saved values. On change it updates the saved pair. Copies all 64 bytes to $F440 when the camera term is zero and enters the three-column recolour loop otherwise.
Low operand of the direct 64-byte template copy at $330C. It comes from the even byte of the pointer selected at $3355.
High byte of the source operand for the template copy at $330C. The loop copies 64 bytes backward into $F440 and skips the recolouring path.
Picks one of the six sprite templates in file K from the pointer table at $3355 and patches the three indexed loads used for its three byte columns.
Copies 21 rows of the selected template into $F440, mapping each source byte through the lookup table at $0568.
Low operand for the first recoloured template column, copied directly from the selected file K pointer.
High byte of the first patched template load in the recolouring loop. $3329 writes the high byte of the selected file K sprite pointer here.
Low operand for the second recoloured template column, set to the first column address plus one.
High byte of the second recolour load's patched source operand. $332C copies it from the chosen template pointer.
Low operand for the third recoloured template column, set to the first column address plus two.
High byte of the patched source operand at $3346. The last byte-column loop translates the fetched byte through $0568, writes it to the destination and moves backward three bytes.
Six 64-byte-aligned source addresses from $FD80 to $FEC0. The caller selects one and patches the three source operands in the recolour loop.
High byte of the first template address. Both readers at $3304 and $3326 use the even pointer index so they get the high byte paired with the corresponding low byte at $3355.
A single $80 after the six two-byte template pointers. The six valid template indices end at $335F/$3360.
Eight masks indexed by slot number. The sprite register updates use the masks to change an individual slot's bit.

Saves the source actor from X. Scans actor indices down from $02, with two extra indices when the high nibble of the ball phase is zero.
