Rejects the source and opponents, then calls $23A0 for the direction and distance. Compares that direction with the actor's facing at $027E and gives close or specially indexed candidates an adjusted rank. Stores the winning unadjusted distance and index in $59 and $62.

Returns when the fixed-camera flag at $076F is set. Otherwise compares the ball's 16-bit X at $0210/$0219 with the camera origin at $0F/$10. Keeps the ball within an offset from $94 through $C5 by moving the camera up to two pixels per call, clamped to $0000–$014E. Rebuilds the court strips when the tile column changes and revisits the scroll buffer when the sub-tile phase crosses the half-cell boundary.

Patches the source of the edge-column copy according to the scroll direction and column. Moves the existing visible cells between the $CC00 and $F000 matrices and fetches the newly exposed column from the two halves at $E000 and $E400.

Copies an edge column using the row-offset table at $362E and the prepatched source and destination in the two indexed instructions. A row flag tells the loop when to increment the high operand bytes.
Low operand of the scrolling edge-column read at $3619. The row offset is applied as Y.
High operand of the scrolling edge-column read. $3624 increments it when the row-offset flags signal a page crossing.
Low operand of the edge-column write at $361C, patched before the row loop to select the destination column.
High byte of the patched edge-column store operand at $361C. The offset carry test at $361F advances this byte and the source page together.
Low bytes of 25 row offsets, starting at 24 times 40 and ending at zero. $3616 uses them as Y offsets for the incoming edge-column copies while X counts down from 24.
First seven low offsets for forward 40-byte row steps, from zero through $F0. The active edge copier at $3616 uses the reverse list through $3646.
One flag per row of the reverse copy. $361F reads it and increments both patched page operands at the flagged steps before copying the next row.
Waits for a safe raster region, clears two fine-scroll state bytes and marks a matrix change. Copies the selected 40-column colour window one row at a time from the 80-column source at $E800.
Returns the original sign bit of A as zero or one in both A and X.

Visits 33 row pointers from $3A14. For each row it copies 39 bytes one address lower, walking forward from the row's second cell. Between rows, when the raster high bit is set, it updates the three fine-scroll bits of $D016 from $13.

Visits the same 33 row pointers but copies 39 bytes one address higher, walking backward from offset $26 to avoid overwriting the source during the overlapping copy. Between rows it applies the same raster-gated fine-scroll update.
Thirty-three little-endian row addresses used by the screen-shift loops at $39A3 and $39E0.
High byte of the first row address at $3A14. Both scrolling routines load from this base with the same even index as their low-byte load.

Uses the actor slot in $22. For pose state zero, clears the restart gate, sets possession and initializes the $0313 timer to four, then follows the direction path. For a nonzero pose with the gate set, advances the phase, clears $23 and sets actor flag bit three. The direction path chooses the controlled slot for the side of $22, uses the reference slot in $0E and writes the direction to $027E for $22.
Eight headings restricted to three, four or five. The paired row at $3ACD maps each entry to its reflection around heading two.
Eight headings restricted to seven, zero or one. Entry by entry, the sum with the first row is four modulo eight.
Third eight-byte row. It contains headings one through four and adjacent heading inputs can share the same result.
Eight-byte fourth row containing headings four through seven. The table ends before the next routine at $3AE5.

Searches downward from the active roster size at $02 for the closest actor on the side opposite $06, skipping both controlled slots. Writes the selected slot to $22 and copies its flags back to $06. An equal score replaces the earlier candidate.

Refreshes the controlled slots with $2146, then measures each actor's distance to the target in $7A/$7B/$7D and stores it at $02E9,Y. The actor flag sign separates the two sides. The scan saves minimum distances in $16/$17 and their indices in $18/$19. Equal distances retain the lower slot index.
Eight low bytes paired with the sign bytes at $3B4F. The resulting offset is zero at headings zero and four, greatest at two and most negative at six.
Eight sign bytes giving the high part of the offsets at $3B47, with $FF in the last three entries.
Eight signed values spanning minus five through plus four. The maximum is at heading four and the sign changes at headings two and six.

Selects the side from the ball's X high byte at $0219 and negates its X velocity. One side subtracts the Y velocity twice from the negated result and the other adds it twice. Both paths join the damped position update at $3BFC.
Continues the left-side two-byte X velocity negation started with SEC and the low-byte subtraction at $3B6A.
Negates the X velocity word in $0246/$024D and adds the Y velocity word in $0254/$025B twice before applying damping.
Subtracts the X velocity from the entry value in A and propagates the borrow through its high byte. It also negates the Y velocity before falling through to the damping and position update.
Arithmetic-shifts the ball's three signed velocity words right once. Adds the reduced velocities to the three position fields, sign-extending the X addition into its third byte at $0219.
Reads the coarse X coordinate at $054F. It clears bit zero, then subtracts four to obtain the even byte index into the court column pointer table.
Selects a 17-cell column using the pointer table at $468E. Converts the vertical coordinate at $0550 to a row index, reads that map byte and dispatches through the table at $3C91.
Low operand of the ball contact dispatch jump. $3C85 patches it from the selected handler pointer.
High operand of the ball contact dispatch jump, copied from $3C92 plus the doubled contact code.
Seventy-one little-endian handler addresses. The routine at $3C63 selects a handler from this table using twice the court map cell code and patches the jump at $3C8E.
High byte of the first handler address at $3C91. The load at $3C88 uses this base with an even index to obtain the selected handler's high byte.
Returns carry clear immediately for cell codes such as $00 and $41.
Checks the shared contact guard, then uses $67 to select and order the coordinate corrections around $433B before updating contact and sound.
Partner to the $20-family response. Its correction at $42ED is applied on the opposite side of the coordinate adjustment sequence.
Applies the shared guard and the fixed sequence $4BA9, $433B, $4BD3, then updates contact.
Jumps into the type-$03 response after its first sub-cell test.
Requires $67 below 4 and the shared guard before applying correction $437C and updating contact.
Uses the same four-unit sub-cell guard with the correction at $43D0.
Performs the $42ED correction between the two coordinate adjustments and then updates contact.
Calls the $42ED correction directly once the contact guard succeeds.
Tests which side of a sloped boundary the in-cell coordinates in $66 and $67 fall on. Selects a correction path according to ball height.
Tests the complementary in-cell slope, using ball height to distinguish its lower and upper responses.
Records contact, selects effect 1 and adds one to the ball's integer Y coordinate.
Compares ball height with $38 before allowing the positive X correction. Below that height it selects the carry-set result at $40FE.
Records the hit, starts effect 1 and increments the ball's horizontal coordinate, propagating carry to its high byte.
Selects among six 16-byte response shapes. Each small entry chooses its shape and passes the result to the common routine at $3F6F.
Computes an upper-half cell index and reads the second response table at $4008 before entering the common result handler.
Computes an upper-half cell index and reads the third response table at $4018 before entering the common result handler.
Computes the lower-half cell index and reads the fourth response table at $4028 before processing the result.
Computes the lower-half cell index and reads the fifth response table at $4038 before processing the result.
Computes the lower-half cell index and reads the sixth response table at $4048 before processing the result.
Alternate dispatch target for the first shape response. Uses the upper-half index and reads from $3FF8.
Alternate entry performing the same second-shape lookup as $3EDD, using $4008 as its base.
Alternate entry for the third shape response. The upper-half index selects the byte at $4018 plus X.
Alternate entry for lower-half shape four. The lookup at $3F28 uses base $4028.
Alternate entry for lower-half shape five. The lookup at $3F31 uses base $4038.
Alternate entry for lower-half shape six. The lookup at $3F3A uses base $4048.

Uses local Y minus four as the row within the upper shape half. For a nonnegative result, combines it with twice the even part of local X and returns the lookup index in X. For local Y below four, discards its own return address and exits through the no-contact path at $3FA9.
For local Y below four, combines it with twice the even part of local X to return a table index in X. Otherwise drops its own return address and exits the caller with carry clear at $3FA9.

Saves the incoming result and checks that ball phase and possession are clear, with ball height from $38 through $41. A positive result moves Y one unit, updates velocity through $4B7F and $24DF, then assigns contact code $0A. A negative result enters the scoring setup at $3FAB.

Sets contact code five and phase $50. Places the ball just inside the vertical limit, chooses its side flag from the ball's X high byte and reloads its X coordinate from that side's stored pair. Calls $4A6C and clears the vertical velocity.
Six 16-byte lookup sequences selected by the shape-specific cell handlers at $3ED4-$3F3F.
Last eight response bytes of the first contact shape. The shape begins at $3FF8, with the ledger boundary at $4000.
Sixteen responses for the second contact shape, indexed by the local cell position at $3EE0 or $3F16. A high bit can take the scoring path.
Sixteen responses for the third shape. $3EE9 and $3F1F use the upper-subcell index to read it before testing ball phase, possession and height.
Sixteen lower-subcell contact responses. The last half is zero, which takes the no-contact path through $3F86.
Sixteen responses used by the fifth shape handlers at $3EF8 and $3F2E. Positive two takes the Y increment at $3F99 if the common contact gates accept it.
Sixteen responses for the sixth shape. A response of two is present in five cells of its first half, with the remaining responses zero.
These 88 bytes reproduce $4000 through $4057, starting halfway through the first contact shape and continuing through the last shape used by $3ED4 through $3F3F.
Eight zero bytes after the copied shape slice and before the cell $46 handler at $40B8.
Checks the same ball-height boundary as cell $45 before allowing the negative X correction.
Records the hit and subtracts one from the two-byte ball X coordinate while CPU interrupts are masked.
Returns carry clear when the high vertical delta is negative. Otherwise assigns result 1 at $21 and returns carry set.
Tests the high and low vertical delta, assigns result 2 and returns carry set when the paired condition is met.
Stores result 0 at $21 and returns carry set.
When both ball height and a vertical rate field are negative, samples the SID oscillator and calls the effect twice on one in four low-bit results.

Locates a cell through the column pointer table at $468E using $054F and $0550. Doubles the cell code to read a little-endian pointer at $414D, patches the jump at $414A and restores the actor index from $E2 into Y before jumping.

Last byte of the vertical row adjustment branch. The path beginning at $4133 divides the position by two and subtracts eight for the row. The dispatcher doubles the cell code and patches the indirect target before restoring Y.
Low operand of the actor contact dispatch jump, selected from the pointer table at $414D.
High operand of the actor contact dispatch jump. $4145 patches it before reloading the actor slot in Y.
Seventy-one little-endian handler addresses indexed by the cell code in the actor contact dispatcher at $411D. Destinations return a carry result and some update the actor's counter at $07D2.
High byte of the first contact-handler address. The load at $4142 uses this base with an even index to patch the high byte of the jump.
Clears the per-actor counter at $07D2,Y and returns carry clear.
Increments the actor counter when the height byte is zero and $02FE,Y is nonzero. Otherwise clears the counter. Returns carry clear in both paths.
Returns carry set without updating the actor's state.
Returns carry clear for $67 below four. For the remaining offsets it uses the sign of $055C, returning carry set when that byte is nonnegative.
Sign-test entry for the depth direction at $055C. The direct table entries bypass the local-offset check at $41FC and enter here.
Compares $67 with seven minus $66. For offsets that reach the second test, returns carry set only when $055B is nonnegative.
Sign-test entry for $055B. The descending-diagonal handler also reaches it when seven minus local X is at least local Y.
Compares the two cell offsets in $66 and $67. For offsets that reach the second test, returns carry set only when $055A is nonnegative.
Sign-test entry for $055A. The ascending-diagonal handler also reaches it when local X is at least local Y.
Checks the sign bits of $055A and $055D. Either negative byte leaves carry set.
Checks the sign bits of $055B and $055D. Either negative byte leaves carry set.
Returns carry clear for $67 of four or greater. Otherwise returns carry set when $055D is nonnegative.
Alternate entry for the sign test at $055D. Enters with no need to compare local Y, and returns carry set only for a nonnegative byte.
Swaps the two-byte fields at $0246/$024D and $0262/$0269 using the stack.
Negates both 16-bit fields at $0246/$024D and $0262/$0269 while swapping them.
Calls the entry at $45AD, negates and exchanges the fields at $0254/$025B and $0262/$0269, then calls $45B4.
Calls the entry at $45AD, exchanges the fields at $0254/$025B and $0262/$0269, then calls $45B4.
Takes signed halves x and z of the ball's X and vertical velocity. Writes x minus z to X and negative x minus z to vertical velocity, then increases each new component by half.
Writes x plus z and x minus z from the signed halves of the ball's X and vertical velocity. Increases each result by half through $454D and $458D.

Doubles ball Y velocity, then takes signed halves y and z of that result and the vertical velocity. Writes y minus z to Y and negative y minus z to vertical velocity, increases each result by half, then halves Y.

Doubles ball Y velocity, then takes signed halves y and z of that result and the vertical velocity. Writes y plus z to Y and y minus z to vertical velocity, increases each result by half, then halves Y.
Doubles ball Y velocity first. Takes signed halves x and y of X and the doubled Y, writes x minus y to X and negative x minus y to Y, increases both results by half and then halves Y.
Doubles ball Y velocity first. Uses signed halves x and y of X and the doubled Y to write y minus x to Y and negative x minus y to X. Increases both results by half and then halves Y.
Doubles ball Y velocity first. Uses signed halves x and y of X and the doubled Y to write x plus y to X and x minus y to Y. Increases both results by half and then halves Y.

Doubles the ball's Y velocity at $45AD before taking the signed halves of both horizontal velocity words. Replaces X with half Y minus half X, and replaces Y with their sum. Calls the two velocity adjustment entries and then $45B4.
Arithmetic-shifts X velocity into $68/$69, then adds that signed half to the original word at $0246/$024D.
Arithmetic-shifts Y velocity into $68/$69 and adds the result to the original word at $0254/$025B.
Arithmetic-shifts the vertical velocity word at $0262/$0269 into $68/$69 and adds the result back to that word.
Shifts the Y velocity word at $0254/$025B left once.
Arithmetic-shifts the signed Y velocity at $0254/$025B right once. Takes the initial carry for the high-byte rotate from the sign of that byte.

Compares ball height with one. Only if the CMP gives a negative result and the high byte of vertical velocity is negative does it return with carry set. For the ordinary height range this detects a downward velocity at height zero.
Clears the ball height. Reverses the vertical velocity if negative, damps velocity, calls $4C6F and increments the counter at $0567.

Clears proximity flags at $07AF. For ball phase zero, compares unordered pairs from actor slots one through six. A pair within two coarse Y steps and four coarse X steps sets both proximity flags if either has nonzero $02FE and nonzero height. Clears both $07D9 fields for that pair.
Eight entries that add four to the index modulo eight and therefore map a heading to its opposite. No direct indexed reader points into this block.
Eight fractions paired with the signed integer bytes at $4676. The two half-unit fractions occur at headings two and six.
Integer bytes for the first fixed-point component. With the fractions at $466E, the largest positive value is plus 1.5 and the opposing heading has minus 1.5.
Fractional bytes of the second fixed-point component. Diagonal headings use a quarter or three-quarter fraction, paired with the corresponding sign byte at $4686.
Integer bytes for the second fixed-point component. The paired values point from minus one at heading zero to plus one at heading four, with zero at headings two and six.
Eighty little-endian column pointers at 17-byte intervals into $C000-$C54F. The contact lookup selects the column from the horizontal coordinate.
High byte of the first 17-cell column pointer at $468E. The accesses at $3C71 and $412B index this base by the same even offset as their low-byte reads.
High byte of the column 50 pointer, $C352, in the table at $468E. The court lookup indexes this byte when the column offset is $64.
Begins the movement and contact pass when $076F is zero. Visits actor slots from 6 down to 0.
Adds velocity to the three fixed-point coordinates and clamps the predicted position. Integrates the vertical velocity and derives court lookup coordinates and fractional cell offsets.
High-byte extension for the horizontal ADC at $4766. The store at $474D patches it to zero or $FF according to the sign of the horizontal velocity.
Checks actor flags, calls the contact classifier at $411D, and checks nearby actor slots using differences in projected court coordinates.
Sets actor X's contact flag, copies its side flag and index to $06 and $05, and records the other actor in $08 or $09 according to the side.
Prepares slot zero's contact lookup through $2587 and $3C63 and then branches using the result flags.
Uses the actor index in $E2 to zero both horizontal velocity words.

Marks the actor's $02F7 slot. If the contact counter at $0567 is zero, copies the working coordinates and screen position from $054A through $0550 into the actor arrays. Both paths enter the sprite-coordinate publisher at $4ACF.
Clears both horizontal velocity words for the actor in $E2 and sets bit 0 of its flags at $02A1.

Combines the horizontal velocity bytes in the actor activity field at $02FE, publishes the contact flag and subtracts the camera origin into $02B1/$02B8. It halves the relative coordinate and publishes its low byte at $02AA, using $FF at or beyond the right bound.

Scratch cell index initialized with the adjusted X offset and replaced with the heading returned by the contact table. The successful height test transfers the heading to $027E for the actor gaining possession.
Scratch horizontal separation plus two for a close actor pair. The comparison at $4607 only stores it when that adjusted separation is below five.
Five base offsets at stride five. $4A0F selects one by the adjusted Y difference and combines it with the adjusted X difference to index the heading matrix.

Five rows of five headings indexed by the adjusted Y and X distance between the ball and the candidate actor. $4A36 uses the returned heading if the height test passes and the candidate gains possession.
Row offsets used by $4908. For the three accepted relative screen Y offsets, the values nine, eighteen and twenty-seven select successive rows.

Direction codes for close actors. The lookup at $490C adds a relative screen X index from zero to six to the selected row offset. The loaded region also includes the leading row and the cells outside the lookup's accepted columns.
Negates the signed X velocity word at $0246/$024D and calls $24DF to damp ball velocity.
Negates the signed vertical velocity word at $0262/$0269 and calls $24DF to damp ball velocity.
Negates the signed ball Y velocity at $0254 and $025B, then calls $24DF to damp the velocity before returning.
High operand byte of the low-velocity subtraction at $4B97. It points into page two. The following stores finish negating the Y velocity word before damping it.
Subtracts the slot-zero velocity word $0254/$025B from $0246/$024D in place.
Subtracts the byte at $055C from $055A in place.
Adds $055C to $055A in place.
Adds the two-byte Y velocity at $0254/$025B into the X velocity at $0246/$024D.
Negates the vertical velocity and saves it on the stack, then writes the negated X velocity in its place. Restores the first result as X velocity and calls $24DF.
Exchanges the ball's Y and vertical velocity words with a two-byte negation on each result, then calls $24DF.
Stores the new actor height at $023D,Y and copies it to $0551. Clears the height fraction and both vertical-velocity bytes for Y.

Stores the incoming floor at $0551. If it is strictly above the ball height at $023D by the BMI/BEQ tests, raises the ball to that floor. A negative vertical velocity then goes through the reversal at $4B7F and another damping pass. A nonzero vertical high byte after those calls requests voice 1 phase six.
If $05 is nonzero, uses $06 to select $08 or $09 and increments that actor's counter at $07A2. Clears $05 before returning.
Ten minimum oscillator samples indexed by the roster parameter at $13BD. $609E rejects a sample below the selected value.
Projection flag updated with the side's contact flag. A negative value makes $4DC9 replace the projected bearing using the saved heading at $4C8E.
Saved facing of the controlled actor. The projection code uses it if the flag at $4C8D is negative.
Uses ball state, slot state and the SID oscillator readout to choose a timer or movement for a computer-controlled actor. Active timers can return before the remaining steering calculations.

Scores the controlled actor and other actors of its side using nonnegative ball-relative X separation and a direction-distance estimate. If another actor's score plus four is less than the controlled actor's score, writes four to the side's $49 counter and takes the stationary movement path.
First oscillator upper bound used by the computer counter update at $5085. The remaining bounds start at $5052.
Remaining nine entries of the oscillator upper bounds whose first byte is at $5051. $5085 compares the oscillator against the indexed bound before calling the counter update.

For the active controlled actor on a computer side, tests ball phase $73 and a delay below six. Uses a table threshold indexed by $F3, or entry nine if $F4 is nonzero, to decide whether the SID oscillator byte permits a call to $68D1.

Saves actor X at $B0. For a nonnegative target in $62 it starts the horizontal components with coordinate differences. Actor targets below seven go through the vector solver. Other nonnegative targets use the fixed-point scaling path and initialise the vertical component to $04B0.
Starts the subtraction after loading the ball's vertical velocity low byte at $5157. Subtracts the two-byte step at $B7/$B8 from $0262/$0269 and returns to the Y countdown at $5154.

Caps the variation input in $B2 at $3F and halves it. Selects a coefficient from $13B3, $13D1, $13E5 or $13DB using $07AA and the player index at $0768, then uses repeated addition to set the new variation amount.
Uses bit groups from SID oscillator reads at $D41B to scale the variation and choose its sign for each of the horizontal velocity words.
In action $15, forces the second horizontal component negative when $21 is one and positive when $21 is nonzero and greater than one, if it has the opposite sign.
Uses the current actor's direction code at $027E to read the two horizontal velocity words from $6668 and $6678. Sets variation to $14 and enters the common solver at $50C5.
Sixteen entries giving the shortest distance around a 16-position ring from index three. Entries rise to eight opposite that index at eleven, then descend toward the starting side.

Estimates horizontal distance from the two absolute velocity components, then starts scaling the vector. Uses the target height and velocity fields when the target is an actor, and subtracts $4B from the projected vertical velocity per iteration.

Doubles or halves the distance estimate until it crosses $05DC, applying corresponding shifts to both horizontal components. The loop from $5440 refines the resulting components with up to five smaller increments.

Uses a quotient obtained by repeated subtraction of six, a half-gravity increment and the height difference to calculate the initial vertical velocity. Clamps the high byte of the result to the range $FA through $05 interpreted as signed.
Stores the incoming A and X values in the actor motion fields, clears $02DB,Y and sets bit six of $02A1,Y. Advances the ball phase before returning.

Uses actor slot $22 and the incoming direction in X. Scales the two direction components by the word from $20DE indexed through the actor setting at $139E. Stores twice the first result at $0246/$024D and the second result at $0254/$025B for the selected actor.
Adds two in decimal mode to the appropriate two-byte score at $37-$38 or $39-$3A. The XOR of $21 and $1F selects the team. Refreshes scores and advances the ball phase.

Clears the two horizontal ball velocity words and clamps negative X to zero. Sends Y at or above the value in $0232 to the lower-boundary handler. The remaining route tests the court and side before selecting the sloped or upper boundary.
Uses the ball's X high byte to select the sloped boundary formula. The left side writes X low as $DE minus the ball's Y byte. The right side adds Y to $01CA and stores both X bytes.
Immediate $DE operand of the LDA at $55FF, used by the left-side boundary subtraction.

Places the ball's Y coordinate on the selected boundary from $56F4 and clamps its X word to the limits held at $1C44/$1C48 and $1C45/$1C49. One court applies an additional X placement rule based on $053A.
Either branches to the sloped-boundary calculation or clamps the X word using the limits at $1C46/$1C4A and $1C47/$1C4B. The clamp path sets Y to $C0, then advances the ball's phase.
Four Y limits indexed by the court number at $FF24. The ball placement code reads the selected byte at $55F5 and $561E.

Reads a scheduled line from $03C3 and an operation from $03DB. Flagged operations set a sprite's Y coordinate and the others update its pointers in both screen matrices. On exhaustion it restores $575B and sets the next IRQ to raster $F0.
Restores the main raster vector at $FFFE-$FFFF and sets $D012 to $F0 before acknowledging the IRQ and returning.

Dispatches on the raster line. During the split near $F1 it selects the score font at $D000 and blanks the background, then schedules line $FB. At the later interrupt it restores the court view and updates sprites and match work.
Restores the court background from $EFFD, installs fine X scroll and multicolour mode, selects the active screen matrix and updates the raster tick at $E1.
Saved indicator code read by the sprite routine at $5A15. Nonzero values below fourteen select an offset and value for the indicator sprite byte.

Walks the occupied entries in $043C from index $C8 down to one. Appends raster lines to $03C3, sprite selectors to $03DB and Y or pointer bytes to $03F3. Updates VIC positions, colours and sprite pointers, and arms the queue IRQ when it has multiple requests.
For a positive queue index in $E0, installs IRQ $56F8 and schedules the first entry one raster line before its target.

After enabling interrupts, calls $270E and $288B in both paths. Bit zero of $E1 selects the motion pass or the scroll routine. In the scroll path, a clear bit one also calls the sprite compositor update and restores the display enable bit.
Fourteen offsets three bytes apart into the sprite at $F400. The IRQ uses indices one to thirteen and saves the offset of the updated byte so it can clear it at the next update.
Fourteen multicolour byte values paired with the offsets at $5ABF. The IRQ writes the selected value at $5A25.

Takes the reference slot in A and preserves the caller's X for $5B46. Writes the reference actor's X divided by four plus $20 at $8E. At $5B1B the corresponding Y divided by two plus $20 goes to $8F before the heading comparison.

Saves the number of velocity steps from X and patches the predicted actor index from Y into $5B22. Converts the active actor position to coarse reference coordinates before predicting the target position and mapping the heading to a direction mask.

Immediate operand of LDY at $5B21, patched from the target index by $5AFE. The following calculation advances the target position repeatedly by its signed velocity and compares it with the active actor's position.
Uses the active actor index at $D7 to read its state from $0200 and patch the destination of the jump at $5BA7. The selected handler updates the slot for the sprite compositor.
Low operand of the pose dispatch jump at $5BA7, selected by doubling the actor's state.
High operand of the pose dispatch jump, patched from the high byte of the chosen pose handler.
Twenty-four little-endian targets for actor states $00 through $17. The dispatch at $5B94 doubles the state, reads the low byte here and uses the corresponding high byte at $5BAB to patch $5BA7.
High-byte base of the pose handler table. The indexed read at $5BA1 uses the same even index as the low-byte read at $5B9B.

Counts down the actor's pose timer and clears three pose flags when the timer is negative. Advances a six-step fractional animation phase for a nonzero $02FE entry. Selects pose state $0B for the possessor, $15 when either of two event flags is set, or $08 for the flagged or eligible controlled actor before entering the pose selector at $6193.

Selects pose offset zero and clears $0794,Y. Applies the placement handler when the actor has possession. Fire changes the actor state to three and enters the pose selector immediately. Otherwise a nonzero movement byte advances the state and sets ball vertical velocity to $FC00 when the increment reaches two or above. The path then clears the actor state and delay if the actor lacks possession, and sets state $15 if either event byte at $07AF,Y or $07D9,Y is nonzero.

For a moving actor advances the fractional pose counter, wrapping the integer count at six, then adds eight to choose the pose. For a stationary actor chooses pose six or seven from the ball height and vertical speed. Raises the ball above the actor when the height comparison allows it, releases possession when vertical speed reaches zero, and applies fire and event transitions before the common pose selector.
Sets placement selector fourteen and decrements the timer of slot $D7. At zero, advances the state and calls $663E. The actor in $05 selects state eleven before the hand-off to $6193.

Sets the pose selector to three. If the actor's $0552 value reaches its height at $023D, changes the state to ten and sets the timer to six. The actor in $05 selects state eleven, and a nonzero $07AF event overrides either result with state $15.

Selects pose fourteen, sets the actor flag at $0794 and calls $6434. Counts down the timer for slot $D7. On expiry clears the current actor's state, timer and flag. Selection as the actor in $05 overrides the state with eleven before entering $6193.

Places the ball using selector zero and evaluates the selected target slot in $62. A negative index or an index below seven selects state four. Otherwise movement, distance, heading and an oscillator comparison choose state twelve or seventeen, with state five as the fallback. All four paths set a two-tick timer and a variant at $07AA before entering $6193.
Threshold bytes indexed by roster attributes in the two probability tests at $5E18 and $5E5A.
Expected facing values for $5E4C when the selected target slot is greater than seven. The candidate heading at $63 selects one of four ordinary headings followed by four $0F sentinels.
Expected facing values for $5E42 when the selected target slot is seven. Four entries are the $0F sentinel.
Applies placement selector one. When the active slot timer expires, switches the actor to state seven with six ticks, sets $078C, clears $05 and calls $508E with the active slot in X.
Applies placement selector fourteen and counts down the current slot. At zero advances the actor state and calls $663E.
Applies selector three and updates the ball placement. If the actor's high vertical velocity byte is zero or negative, sets state $10, clears $05 and invokes the launch helper $508E.
Applies selector fourteen and decrements the timer. At expiry advances the state, increments both actor flags at $0794 and $079B and calls $63BC.

Applies pose three and tests the high vertical velocity byte. Zero or a negative value advances the state, starts a four-tick timer, changes to pose $10 and calls $508E. Both paths call $6443 with the resulting pose.
Updates placement with selector $10, advances the active state at countdown zero and hands off to $6193.

Selects pose offset $11, sets ball vertical velocity to $FE0C, advances the current actor's state and clears its two event bytes. Copies X and Y from the ranked actor in $62 into the ball slot, masking interrupts around the two X stores. Clears ball possession and both horizontal velocity words before applying the pose.
Sets selector $11. When the actor threshold at $0552,Y is at least the current height at $023D,Y, writes state ten with a six-tick timer, then joins $6193.
Applies placement selector five. At timer zero advances the actor state and writes $03E8 as the actor's vertical velocity before the update at $6193.
Applies selector $12. Advances the state when the vertical velocity high byte subtracts two with a negative result.
Applies selector $13. A negative vertical velocity high byte advances the state, sets a four-tick timer, calls $508E and clears the selected actor byte at $05.
Selects $14. Decrements the timer in slot $D7 and sets state $10 for Y when it reaches zero.

Selects pose one, sets $0794 and clears both horizontal velocity words for Y through $6434. Decrements the timer for $D7. At zero, clears the state, timer and $0794 for Y before the pose update at $6193.

Sets the actor flag at $0794 and clears horizontal velocity. Selects the ball-placement variant from the difference between ball height and actor height. During timer value two, phase zero allows a roster-dependent SID probability check that can switch the actor to state seven and write ball velocity from the facing table. Otherwise places the ball and counts the actor's $0313 timer down toward state one.

Selects pose offset $16, writes seven to $6D and sets the current actor's event byte at $07A2,Y. Clears possession when it belongs to this actor, then jumps over the velocity negation to the height comparison at $6122.

Negates both 16-bit horizontal velocity words for actor Y. The shared tail uses the sign of the predicted-minus-current height comparison at $6128 to decide whether to set vertical velocity to $01F4. It advances the active actor's state on either branch before applying the pose.

Selects pose $16 and, if bit one of $E1 is clear, adds the saved turn at $07D9 to the actor's heading modulo eight. If the subtraction from $0552 of $023D leaves bit seven clear, starts voice 2 phase one, advances the state and sets a ten-tick timer.
Selects pose $15, sets $0794 and applies placement at $6434. Clears the actor's saved turn and $07D2, then decrements the active timer. A negative result selects state ten with timer one.

Updates the facing offset through $629A, then uses the active actor's facing and action index $8A to look up base and overlay pose selectors. It tracks the two mirror decisions at $0328 and $032F. A changed selector or mirror flag sets the actor's rebuild byte at $077E,Y before the new selectors and flags are saved.
Seven countdown bytes, one per slot. The pose path decrements a running count or starts it at three when the oscillator's low six bits are zero.
Ten roster parameters. A zero exits before the short pose-eight countdown and oscillator check. A nonzero value permits the checks when the actor's $0285 flag is set.

Selects turning limits using the actor field at $02FE,Y. Decrements the target-refresh timer at $07CB,Y and can choose a new target at $07C4,Y from the tables at $638C or $639C using the oscillator. It updates the saved angular step at $07BD,Y toward the table-selected offset, then adds it to the actor's facing modulo eight and stores $0285,Y.
Calls $23A0 using Y from $D7 and saves the returned bearing in $07B6,Y for that actor.
Compares the current actor side in $02A1 with $1F and returns seven or eight in A and X for the corresponding side.
Maps the wrapped difference between two actor headings to its signed representative from minus three through plus four. $6336 compares that value with the current offset.

First sixteen entries of the overlapping 32-byte window used at $62E3 when another actor holds the ball. These include eight zero entries, slots one through seven, and $FF. Its upper half shares the first sixteen bytes of the table beginning at $639C.

Thirty-two outcomes for the active ball possessor, indexed by the SID oscillator's low five bits at $62FA. The result at $07C4,Y is either negative for no target, slot seven for the side-dependent reference, or a numbered actor slot.

Uses $62 to select a target. Computes its X and Y offsets from slot zero, multiplies each signed difference by ten, and stores the resulting motion words in the slot indexed by Y. Sets the vertical velocity to $04E2.
Gets the heading between the actor in Y and the selected actor in $62. Restores Y from the active slot $D7 and writes the direction mask to $027E,Y.
Clears both bytes of each of the two horizontal velocity components for actor slot Y.
Doubles the selector in $8A to read a target address from $6459 and patch the jump at $6456. Takes the offset-table index from $027E,Y before entering the selected handler with the actor slot in Y.
Low operand of the placement dispatch jump. $644A writes it from the handler table after doubling the placement selector.
High operand of the placement dispatch jump, copied by $6450 before the dispatcher loads the heading index.
Twenty-three little-endian targets for the ball-placement selector. Several selectors share handlers, and the unchanged-position path at $6487 returns immediately.
High byte of the first handler address. The load at $644D uses this base with an even index to patch the high byte of the jump.
Returns without changing the ball coordinates or motion fields.
Starts with the selected actor's height plus $20 and enters the shared placement path at $649D.
Starts with the selected actor's height plus $0E.
Copies the selected actor's position to slot zero with offsets from $2C5D/$2C65 and $2C6D. Copies the actor's three velocity words into the ball fields.
Starts with the selected actor's height plus six and reuses the placement path at $649D.
Starts with the selected actor's height plus eleven and reuses the placement path at $649D.
Starts with the actor's height plus $1C. Uses the offsets from $2C76/$2C7E and $2C86 before copying the three velocity words.
Places the ball relative to the selected actor using $2C8E/$2C96 and $2C9E. Clears the ball's two horizontal velocity words.
Places the ball with the same offset tables as $652C and copies both horizontal velocity words from the actor.
Uses $65FE/$6606 and $660E for position offsets and $6616 for a height correction. Adds $15 to the resulting height and copies the actor's motion.
Uses $661E/$6626 and $662E for position offsets and $6636 for a height correction. Adds $15 to the resulting height and copies the actor's motion.
Eight low bytes for the X offset added at $65A4.
Last two low-byte offsets in the eight-position array beginning at $65FE. The table's paired high bytes start immediately after them.
Eight high bytes for the X offset added with carry at $65AC.
Eight Y offsets read at $65B7.
Eight height offsets read at $65C1 before adding the fixed $15.

Eight Y offsets read at $65E9.
Eight height offsets read at $65F3 before adding the fixed $15.
Doubles the selected actor's parameter at $13C7,Y to index a vertical launch speed in $6654. Copies the low and high bytes to the actor and preserves X.
Low byte of the first in a sequence of little-endian launch speeds spaced by $32. $6645 doubles the roster parameter and reads both halves with that index.
High byte of the first launch speed. $664B reads this and subsequent high bytes with the same even index as the low-byte load.
Low byte of the first of eight little-endian ball X speeds. $52A1 indexes these by twice the actor heading.
High byte of the first of eight signed ball X speeds. $52A7 reads this base using the same even index as the low-byte load.
Low byte of the first of eight little-endian depth speeds. $52AD loads the selected byte and $52B0 stores it in the ball velocity field at $0254.
High byte of the first of eight signed ball Y speeds. $52B0 stores the selected byte in the ball's $025B high velocity field.

Converts X to units of eight pixels. For the active actor it uses the working X at $7A/$7B, otherwise it reads the slot indexed by Y. Reflects the coordinate about $53 when the side bit differs from $1F. For slot zero the caller supplies the side in A.

On a zero delay at $23, takes the slot from $22. For slots one and above, sets the position to X=$024F and Y=$D2 and initializes its restart targets. For slots where slot plus four is below seven, places the other actor's target according to side and the two coordinate tables at $1CFA and $1D00. Decrements the slot and delays the next placement, or advances the restart phase when the adjusted index is one.

Returns when the active side has a nonzero decision latch at $49,X. Starting with the candidate in $08,X, it takes a same-side candidate other than the current actor, measures bearing and distance at $5AFC, and compares nearby opposing actors' bearings and distances against the candidate's. If it passes the tests, sets the side's decision latch through $68C7 and sends the bearing through $2388 to $2013. Candidate indices six and below take the opponent scan, and indices seven and up take the alternate checks at $6841.

Requires the candidate distance in X to be below $28. Checks the opposing side's saved actor and, when its $02E9 field is at least $10, combines an indexed mask from $6867 with the SID oscillator byte before joining the accepted path at $6835.
Seven masks that progressively admit zero, one or two oscillator bits. The pass check selects one with the coarse counter divided by eight.
Twenty-four signed X increments indexed by fine bearing. $4DD3 adds the selected increment to the coarse target coordinate for each iteration of the projection loop.
Twenty-four signed Y increments paired with $686E. $4DDB adds the corresponding increment to the coarse Y coordinate.
Converts projected distance zero through fourteen into a decreasing score from twelve to zero. $4F4A uses it after the range and side adjustments in the nearby-actor scan.
Eight fine-bearing indices at stride three, selected by $4DCC when the projection uses the actor's eight-way heading.
Normalizes a signed bearing difference by adding or subtracting 24 until it falls in the range zero through 23.
Extracts the side index from the sign bit of $8C and stores two in that side's $49 slot.
Increments $3F when $8C has bit seven clear and $40 when it is set. A wrap of $3F to zero falls through and increments $40 as well.
Clears $3F or $40 according to bit seven of $8C.

A's sign selects the side. Returns carry set for a detected fire input. A negative synthetic input flag suppresses fire and a positive nonzero one asserts it. Otherwise chooses between the active-low CIA fire bit and the side's computer fire flag, based on the side's controller setting.
Clears the first $2F VIC registers, sets $D011 and $D018 for a blank display and assigns background colour 1.
Sixty-three sprite bytes at the end of file B. Match initialization copies the 64-byte slot to $F400, including the following routine's first opcode $A5 as the unused last byte.

Lower bounds for indices one through nine in the comparison at $69BA. The indexed read starts one byte earlier at the RTS opcode at $69DA, so index zero reads $60.

Exclusive upper bounds for indices zero through nine. The comparison at $69BF takes the return path when the stored oscillator sample masked to seven bits meets or exceeds this bound. The first entry is also the lower bound for index nine.

Last 19 bytes of file B. They overwrite the corresponding bytes of the ninth original catalogue from file A. Both oscillator threshold lookups stop before this tail, with their largest index fixed to nine.
